I saw VN’s who use lot’s of free assets and are charging much more. This prize is more than fair.
A clear recommendation. If you like a good story or you are a VN fan then this is for you. The only thing I don’t like is the shortage of keyboard shortcuts and having only 5 saving slots (maybe that’s intentional.)
With this we are introduced into the world and history of the Echos of the Fey. A perfect opening and introduction to our main character Sofiya.
Sofya Rykov is a private investigator with a penchant for drinking too much and avoiding unpleasant serious personal stuff. This fact is made very clear in the beginning as she laughs away her traumatic experience in Onigrad. I becomes very apparent that she isn’t just a one dimensional character “who just loves to have fun”. Her actions and behaviour makes sense. She has her own packet to carry and life wasn’t very gentle to her. Thus she has her own voice, just like the rest of the cast.
And that’s what impressed me the most. Nearly every character has a sprite - side characters aren’t just some talking sprites that gives the player information. They have their own motivation, their own thoughts and thus their own ethics and morality. They aren’t just some blank characters who the MC can influence like some Bioware characters. They will act on their own manners. That doesn’t mean that we can’t completely influence them. This VN managed to flesh the characters out so well that they feel like a real person and everyone has something interesting to say. Never have I meant such interesting side characters in VN who are right now on the market.
Unlike most other VNs the decision we make here matters. It’s rare to see a Vn where choosing which decision to pick makes you sweat. It will have consequences and you are expect to clean up the mess you made for the most part. You simply can’t save anything at once and can’t satisfy everyone. Once you picked a path you should stick to it.  That sounds more disastrous and depressing than it is. I just want to warn people that the game doesn’t take making tough decisions from you.
The setting is a nice mix between magic and Steampunk, with a hint of Final Fantasy. It’s unique in it’s own way without being obnoxious and the superb writing really helps. The writing and the worldbuilding is consistent and is really, really well done. The art is also very consistent. Everything feels fresh since the different Art, the GUI, the backgrounds and the music is made by the developers. No more Kevin Macleod music that has been used to death. All in all, it makes it very easy to get immersed into the game and it’s world.
Playing detective is fun, too. I should explain to you the game mechanics. The game is a mix of a Visual Novel and a Side-scroller. Dialogs and decisions are done and presented in a typical VN manner (Dialog box on the bottom, speaking Characters in the background, option boxes in the middle of the screen, see screenshots). Then there is the part we can walk around Vodotsk. We can enter shops and other locations by walking around the town and clicking on the doors or talking to people on the streets. The game has a map, an inventory and a quest log. We can walk around town as Sofiya or in our cat form. This helps with our research. People who play adventure games will feel at home here. And newcomers can easily catch up. The game is not to hard, but not to easy. The game will let you know on what to do so you will never feel lost, but also manages to not treat you like an Idiot. You are still expected to read and comprehend what you just read. Otherwise solving the case will be hard for you when you are expected to piece together all informations.
Uff, I hope I wasn’t rambling too much and thank you for reading. I hope my english writing wasn’t too horrible.

Now this is my first review I've written so yeah.
This game has taken a crap ton of hours from me, for better or for worse, and what I've noticed from those hours is that patience can be very rewarding, mostly gameplay wise. I've had this game since the latest update 31 came out, and haven't really had any of the problems I've noticed others have had, I'm not gonna name them cuz I am lazy. The gameplay is probably the most open and captivating that I have seen in a game to date, and offers a lot of possibilities and methods of victory. This is aided by the fact that the terrain is destructible, buildings and other fortifications feel "concrete" and wear away over the battle as does the battle field, covered in blood and machine and vehicle parts, and the gameplay mechanic of orbital delivery adds a sense of urgency/excitment to offensive attacks and defensive counter attacks. That said, the gameplay mechanics build up the game, and make it worth playing, now thats not to say that more couldn't hurt, like day and night cycles with the darkness of night adding stealth mechanics and sneak attacks, perhaps a custom weapon maker, firing crabs out of a gun, or maybe water, underwater bases, water traps, water water... these of course aren't necessary but they would add a bunch to the game, and the need for updates is also a concern for me, but hey, if they are on hiatus then so be it.
As for its gameplay mechanics such as controlling mass amounts of units and stuff like that it is probably the most innovative I've ever played before, I can be very fun with friends or solo, and once you get used to how the little guys play you'll be setting up sqauds, fortifying your base, hunting for brains, and blowing things up in no time. As for play and replayability, it truly depends on what kind of  system specs you have, if you have a lot of ram opened up, then it should run fairly smoothly, just dont get mods that'll crash the game, and for replayability, if you download some scenarios it can be very worth it, all in all, its a good game with a couple rough edges like not enough maps or slow moving guys but the positives out weigh the negatives from my experiance, so I'd reccomend it.

The Witcher 2 was my first introduction to Geralt.
If you're interested in a rich story, with lots of lore behind it than this is the game for you. I came into the game knowing nothing about the Witcher universe and I hadn't played the first game before it.
It doesn't do much to hold your hand when it comes to introducing you to the world. Characters simply start speaking about passed events and political situations which the player has no knowledge of. For me this was actually a great thing, it made me feel like the world had a lot more going on in it than you'll ever know about.
As for gameplay, it was decent, the newest entry in the series surpassed it in many ways, but this one was still a great ride. The bold decision to close off an entire third of the game to you based on a decision at the end of the first act was one that's stuck with me. On subsequent playthroughs you'll be able to explore your choices and see new areas. Unlike the open world of the witcher 3, this closed world meant that the section of the game really is closed off, and not just somewhere you could walk to on your own. Because of this huge impact on the experience of the game based on your choices, I still think this is one of my favourite games I've ever played.
While it did come out quite a while ago, there has been an active mod community that pumped out some great mods and graphic improvements. Check them out to make the game a little more up-to-date graphics and interface wise.
Couldn't recommend it more. It is a fantasy world, adult action game, so if you don't want sex, violence, explicit language or sword combat in your games, then skip it. Otherwise jump on in.

Perfection. For years there's been a lack of an offically liscensed Monster Jam game,Path Of Destruction was the last one,met with negative criticism back in 2009. Yeah,it's been 6 years. And it seems like yesterday i was unboxing that one! Well,here we are,Monster Jam Battlegrounds,the next gen era of gaming containing such classics as Skyrim,Metal Gear Solid V : The Phantom Pain,Gran Turismo and Forza 6,Infamous: Second Son,and a ton more,and now we have a Monster Jam game to match.
Pros:
they FINALLY got the engine sound right! For years we've been hearing that dying go-kart noise in the games,but now these new devs have taken REAL audio clips from various shows,and merged them all into that classic,awesome noise we all love. The best sound design to date in any of these games.
The physics. This game is like Rigs Of Rods,but with all but a few glitches removed,actual damage,decent sounds and effects (such as exhaust and lights),and an updated selection of the biggest names on the scene,including El Toro Loco,Grave Digger,Monster Mutt,NEA,El Diablo's 2014 design,Bounty Hunter's new look,that Madusa truck,Son Uva Digger,Lucas Oil Crusader,and that's just the tip of the iceberg. The physics as well as this new selection makes it a MASSIVE improvement. Oh,and it's offically liscensed too,something else it has over ROR. I like to know that when i buy a game and play with Monster Jam trucks,that the money i spent is going to the people actually behind it. Not something most people think about,but it can't hurt to mention.
Commentary. THANK YOU so much for the commentary! Older games would have at most 5 clips on repeat,and it was obvious. Some didn't even have commentary at all. Not a lot of people know this,but when you go to a Monster Jam show,you actually CAN hear the commentary from where you sit,assuming you listen hard enough over the loud engines. And this game,though it doesn't have many more clips that the others,manages to use them in a way that fools the mind,making it seem like fresh,new dialouge. It seems impossible,but one or two plays and you'll see what i mean.
The credits and upgrade system. In this game,it's possible to play effectively without upgrading trucks,but if you do,that makes them more resistant to damage,gives them slightly easier handling (which is IMPORTANT considering what i'm gonna talk about later),and on the side their boost and acceleration get little power-ups as well! You get credits for doing events,based on how good you did. That's another thing,the computer is REALLY good at judging your runs,and giving you the stars according to how many you would get realistically. More stars,more points. You can spend the credits on new trucks AND upgrades. But don't worry,you get Madusa,Lucas Oil Crusader,and Bounty Hunter from the start.
The events: Lots of people will probably disagree,but i like the events in this game. There are 3 categories: Skill Driving,Stunt Driving,and Stadium Events. Stadium events are your basics,Racing and Freestyle,at tons of stadiums from Angel Stadium to AT&T Stadium to of course Sam Boyd Stadium where the finals takes place. These are the only ones that allow you to actually steer your truck. Too bad to,because in the other 2 types,your truck WILL spin out at some point,i guarantee it,and the AI bot put in charge of steering is honestly TERRIBLE at it. you'll spend a good 10 full seconds stumbling and sliding around trying to get the bot to steer the truck forward again. But with good use of Air control,you can avoid this. Oh yeah,they added Air Control,and someone finally got it right! you can use W and S to tilt your truck forward or backwards. This is a must-have unless you want to total your truck.
Now the 2 types of events that this game surprisingly got a lot of hate for. Skill driving is your basic 2D platformer,it shares it's 5 track themes with Stunt Driving,Frozen,Farm,Urban,Forest,Desert. Get across the track in time to get at least 1 star without totaling your truck or your toast. From what i understand,people hate these and Skill Driving because their outside the stadium,but i think it's an EXCELLENT idea. Monster jam has done "Monsters On The Beach","Monsters In The Snow",and "Back To School Bash" for YEARS now,all taking place outside of any offical stadium,but still allowing for great jumps and stunts. That's basically the exact same thing as these events.
Stunt driving is like skill driving,but it isn't just get across the map,this time you have to do 1 of 3 goals,which you will see before you start the level. Destruction requires you to destroy at least 3 cars and make it to the finish,Jump requires you to slowly inch your way through the map,blasting the gas when you hit a massive drop so you fly a certain distance to the finish,and then there's precision,where you jump for one of three targets. I couldn't help but laugh at one of these when i didn't even get the easy goal,and was greeted with the message,"CONGRAGULATIONS,YOU GOT THE NONE GOAL." I know i'm making these sound easy and dull from my descriptions,but they surprisingly require TONS of skill and practice. Chances are,you'll be playing at least one of these 3 times before you beat it.
Trading Cards - always a nice touch
Decent Zombie: this game uses the pre-2015 zombie look. Any monster jam nerd will know,they seriously dumbed down the look of the zombie truck in 2015,to avoid scaring the growing younger audience. However,for zombie nerds all over,it was a let down to see what was once such a dramatic,dark looking truck turned into what looked like something made out of play-doh. However,this game returns to the exposed brain,red spots,and that classic glossy finish on the paint. THIS is a zombie.
Now onto the cons:
- Automatic Assists
Now i know what your thinking,"The game's aimed at kids,won't these help them to enjoy the game despite their younger minds?". Well,yes it will. However,there's an "Expert" mode,that supposedly gives you full control of your truck,and even then these can't be disabled. Their only in the Stadium events luckily. I managed to get around them by slowly inching my way around the track,and only really flooring it when i wanted to jump,but i wish they would have let the amazing physics of the game shine through as players really got to feel the real potential of the trucks,instead of basically forcing us to just hold the up arrow until a bar is full. If you get one of these,my best advice is to slam on the brakes,and wait for it to go down. BUT that can DESTROY your performance,because the whole time limit thing.
- Impossible levels
I have been playing this game non-stop since it was released,and i found impossible levels. Not incredibly difficult ones,but literally impossible. As in,i have messed around with them for what feels like weeks now,using air control,pressing all the buttons,and i can not find a way to possibly get past some of the stuff they throw at me impossible. The game is aimed at kids,yet an adult couldn't beat these or predict some of the random obstacles they throw right outta nowhere. Luckily,due to the way the game is built,you don't HAVE to do these to unlock more levels,you just have to get a certain amount of points to unlock new levels,so you can work around them in your playthrough and save some frustration. Here is a list of the levels that were like this.
Skill Driving - Extreme Forest
Skill Driving - Extreme Desert
Skill Driving - Medium Farm
Skill Driving - Extreme Frozen
As you can see,most of these were Extreme levels,and all of them were in Skill Driving. I don't know if i'm missing something,or if the play testers are just amazing,or if it was a mistake or what,but i seriously can not figure out what to do in these,or how i'm supposed to get going fast enough without flying off the second i hit a bump in the road.
4/5 stars,a must buy for anyone into racing simulators.

What better way to prove you're a real man then playing a game with Monster trucks... All the excitement of being at a live monster truck show. The crunching of cars, the shattering of glass, and the roar of a huge engine being driven by a 50 year old slightly balding man in a blue jumpsuit...
roar... starting this game up I was drawn back to my days as a lad. Watching my 21 inch television, the screen flickering occasionally, looking at huge monster trucks, barreling down a dirt track toward a ramp... hitting that ramp and falling directly on top of 4 or 5 car shells... Crushing them immediately under the weight of the 4 ton monster truck...
Starting the game up I was quickly disappointed by the fact the game seems rather bare bones. Although thinking about it, how many different ways can you set up crushing cars..
Once started up, you have 3 options to choose from....
You have skill driving (which is pretty much a direct copy of Trials) this requires you to drive around on a locked track, hit ramps where you can do tricks... This works well with a motorcycle, but not so much with a Monster truck.. All the awesome tricks stuffed into Trials aren't present in Monster Jam, instead you just hit the A button and hope you have enough steam to climb the next hill... or when you hit a ramp your truck doesn't flip on it's hood...
Arena mode - ahh Arena mode, you race an invisible truck around a track. The track is fairly basic, with one sometimes two ramps, a few cars around. The track doesn't tither you to a straight line as much as skill driving... but... the steering is crap. You feel like you're being held on a string and only allowed to deviate off the destined path slightly or else you lose..
Last of all you have Stunt mode, which well i'm guessing it's nearly the same as Skill driving only with points being awarded for you doing stunts?
all of them are pretty boring and uninspired. It's just a matter of hitting the drive button, and waiting for the win screen to pop up... Unless you magically flip over your truck and lose... Trust me it's boring..
The game play is set up in nearly an identical way as Trials, you advance to harder difficulty settings by getting a set number of stars, stars are rewarded for completing tracks in a timely manner. I guess it could be fun if you are into repetitive game mechanics and boring game play.
The only positive aspect of the game was the officially licensed Monster trucks.. the game has 23 officially licensed trucks including some like Grave Digger, which even non Monster Truck fans will recognize. So if you're big into monster trucks maybe consider buying it for that reason.
The bottom line is... unless you are a huge monster truck fan, or want to own a game which will eventually be removed from steam (officially licensed trucks) I'd avoid this game. Even if you're a huge fan of Trails, this game won't fill that void, it'll just come across as a cheap knock off trying to cash in on using officially licensed monster trucks..
Save your money for something else, unless you can find it for under a buck... then it may be worth it for the Trading cards alone... Surely not worth a full price purchase...

My decision not to recommend this game comes from the high price tag.  With only a couple hours of content before completing the game 100% I've come to have a bit higher expectations in mid 2015.  Not to say I always measure games by their playtime.
Visually the game looks like PS2 era which does not help the case.  While the game modes are fun but short, the ones I enjoyed most were the shortest. You are forced to play through them all in campaign earning stars to advance usually achieving highest rank on first try.
The stadium mode reminds me of the Monster Jam live events, there are only a hand full of arenas though and a lap is never more than 30s with only 3 rounds to win the event.  The stadium events offer freestyle mode as well which feels like button mashing in a racing game or hurling your truck into jumps to pull of tricks.  The game also has side scrolling game modes in the trials style of balancing front and back as well as speed to make your way through obstacle courses and jump challenges.  An enjoyable adventure but looking ten years old at release, I say again, its hard to justify such a price tag.

Zup! 1 was OK and kinda fresh, Zup! 2 was better with its circular agent, but Zup! 3 gets old and boring fast, with nothing new but (-sorry-) idiotically duplicated achievements; for one level there is a dozen of earned "achievements", half of them being granted for opening the level, half of them for passing it; they all bear the letter or character of the level as name, with only different colors. That's it; no achievement for special feat, for "more-efficient-than-average" success, nothing.
I understand why the Zup! series has over-the-top ratings; it's difficult to "not recommend" these games as they provide some relaxing time and players don't expect much for so little money.
But don't be fooled by Steam's binary rating, Zup! games aren't great puzzle games either; they are based on a simple but effective idea, and provide none to mild puzzle challenge. – The "no challenge" part is much more prevalent than one would expect; many levels are litterally just a display of physics chain reaction in this minimal setting without deduction neither meaningful choice involved. Often there are a bunch of explosive blocks to destroy at once by clicking on one of them, and only one triggers the effect that will make the ball land on the green surface; there is no way to deduce which is the right one, you just empirically try one block after the other.
Zup! is a physics sandbox for the the developer to design levels. I'm pretty sure he has more fun designing them than the players playing them, then selling them for a couple of bucks. You should include the level editor and let the community publish their own levels, and then your Zup! game concept, which is a commendable idea, will reach its full potential.

It's difficult to give the information you need in order to make a decision about purchasing the game, since most of the reviews (at least recently) have been either, "BEST GAME EVER" or "PIECE OF CRAP!", and the occasional smart-alek "Recommend 10/10 for being a piece of crap". I feel like people haven't been told the truth about the game, and I hope to fix that in this review.
The game is a dinosaur shooting game, as you might have guessed from the trailers.
But is it fun?
Yeah, it's really hecking fun. Now, I haven't actually played any other FPS co-op survival games, but it is said that the game is highly reminiscent of COD Zombies. If you're into COD Zombies, you might just stick with that. But I found shooting the heads off of raptors with assault rifles, tanks, and many many other weapons very appealing. It's just fun! The same-old mode gets, well, the same after a while. Yes, there are more modes to play, but not all of them are great.
But is the game well made?
I can't exactly say that it is either well made or not. There is certainly a LOT of jank stuff in the game, like getting thrown around the map, or getting your vehicle rolled over. But it's not game-breakingly glitchy, I mean there has never been a "fall-through-the-map" moment or anything like that. The game works.
Going on with the well-madeness of the game, other reviewers have noted that there is a lack of tutorial in the game, and I would have to agree. One particular instance of the lack of tutorial was interacting with the weapons/augments shop. I spend several minutes trying to figure out how to activate it (finding out in time that it is the E key).
The game doesn't get the best frames per second, and is very inconsistent. I've found that it gives better FPS on some maps than others. Intense action with lots of players at your side also contributes to worse gameplay.
The graphics aren't TERRIBLE, but nothing stood out to me in the game. Skyboxes are bland and unconvincing. The weather and time-of-day systems tend to be very sudden changes, with little to no blend at all. Textures are good, but not great. Dinosaur animations aren't the best, and there have been some occasions when big dinosaurs will just sit there and spin around on an axis. Dinosaurs and vehicles don't mix.
Nothing really saves the game from these presentation issues, but one good thing I liked about the game was the soundtrack. That's all I really have to say. I liked it.
And once again, nothing was truly BAD about the game, it's just that nothing is impressive. It's not done, and I wish the developers wouldn't pretend that it is. The game is littered with bugs, and there are hundreds of ways the game could be improved. But for now, it's not BAD.
THE CRITICAL VERDICT:
-Presentation: 4/10. No tutorial mode. Buggy junk.
-Graphics: 5/10. Inconsistent FPS. Textures look good. Nothing impresses.
-Sound: 7/10. I liked the soundtrack. Sound effects are complete, and I'm not left hungry for more sound improvement, though it doesn't impress. Voices for Assault and Recon classes were not good, but the Support class voice was actually pretty entertaining...but still not good.
-Gameplay: 7.5/10. Plays fine. No glitches. It's fun. But once again, the lack of inspiration kind of wears out the formula.
-Lasting appeal: 7.5/10. I took a break from the game for the longest time, but am now coming back to it. It's fun, but it'll wear you out quickly. Achievements are also a plus.
Critical score: 5/10.
So Steam asks me if I would recommend this game. I wouldn't either recommend or discourage buying this game, but when you round up .5 you get 1, so I'll leave it as a thumbs up. The game isn't very well made, but I still had tons of fun playing it.

EDIT: Aug 31, 2017:
---------------------------------------
It's been a year and Stellaris has grown as a game considerably. The addition of Utopia bringing Traditions and Ascension perks make the early game a little more rewarding, while improving the late game via some really powerful perks. Countless balance changes have changed fleet compositions wildly, and new events make the game more flavorful than ever.
However. there is one big caveat. Unity, Traditions, and Ascensions highlight a huge issue with the AI. Namely that they have yet another way to fall behind. Due to suboptimal ship designs, horrible building prioritization, and the inability to keep Tradtions on track due to a lack of Unity production mean that a mildly competent player can run circles around even an "Insane" difficulty AI.
That said, do I still recommend Stellaris? For the most part yes. Stellaris will always shine as a roleplaying 4X before anything else. I look forward to further support for this game and will be aiming to 100% the game for the third time with the new expansion.

A PC port of a PlayStation console game riding off the success of a much better game in FFVII.  This game tries to distance itself from FFVII and tries a lot of new things but all those things just fall flat and make the game a boring grind fest filled with uninteresting characters.  The following review may contain some spoilers.
Let's start off with the story of the game, It's boring and uninteresting.  At no point in time was there ever a feeling of some epic journey or that the world was ever truly in peril.  Even the big evils don't feel very big, your rival is just your rival cause the game told you he was and then nothing important happens with him.  The first big evil is dispatched pretty early in the game and you learn that some distant bigger evil is trying to destroy the world.  The problem is that this new bigger evil isn't ever really there, so it doesn't feel like part of the story, you end up going through the whole game to meet this evil once and that fight feels so anticlimactic because there was never any real conflict with them to begin with.  The worst part of the story is that nothing 'evil' or overly bad happens in the story to make you feel like there's conflict, some place gets blown up with missiles, but you never went there and you only know a single character from there, so when you go to survey the damage, you just kind go there and think "yup, this place sure was blown up", even the character from there doesn't seem to upset about it.  The characters also felt very bland and didn't seem to grow or change, most of them are still the same shell of a character you see right from the start of the game, none of the games events seem to change them, for example one character is the spunky hot head, he remains that throughout the story and is the same cookie cutter character at the end.  You'd think all the death/destruction the team has come across might change him, nope.  The main protagonist does learn/change a bit throughout the story, but going from broody antisocial dope to mildly likeable hero isn't much.  However the biggest offender in this game isn't the story, its the battle system.
This has easily got to be the worst battle system of any Final Fantasy game.  It's pretty standard for how most FF games work, you get 3 characters and they can attack, cast magic, use summon(GF in this game), use items along with a bunch of other abilities that can be learned.  So you acquire these GFs throughout the game, you can level them up and when they level up they give you access to new powers/abilities to make your team stronger such as +% strength/magic/speed/etc, or new abilities like converting cards/items/magic to other things, in/out of battle abilities and more.  GFs also give you the ability to Junction magic to certain stats to give that stat a boost or apply an elemental attack/defense to it, this is where the battle system goes to♥♥♥♥♥♥  In order to get magic, it either has to be drawn from enemies, converted from other sources, upgraded from previous tiers of magic, draw points found on the map and so on.  This ends up being a big, boring and long grind simply to make the game longer.  I tried to play the game at first with just what I drew/acquired but I was spending more time doing that crap than actually progressing through the game, so for everyone else, draw once, then press the F5 button on your keyboard.  F5 gives you max gil and max stacks of magic you have acquired, so you can draw a single Cura for example, hit F5 and get a stack of 100.  It doesn't entirely fix how bad the draw/magic system is, but it lets you ignore it for the most part.  It also lets you have fun with the junction system, which is somewhat enjoyable trying to figure out decent combinations as well finding the right junctions to make some bosses/enemies a bit easier and you really want them to be done with faster cause SquareEnix managed to find a way to make every single fight take as long as possible.
Every single battle animation in this game takes about 10x longer than it should.  Those GFs that you can acquire and equip, yeah, they also have some incredibly stupid long animations if you choose to cast them like a summon from other FF games.  The worst offense is that those animations can not be skipped.  The same goes for a lot of the later higher tier magic that you can acquire as well.  Maybe there was a setting I missed or something that turns all that off, but if there isn't, I suggest you get used to the F1 key on your keyboard.  It lets you speed up the game so you are not sitting and watching the same animations play out over and over again.
I can guarantee that over half my playing hours is because of these unskipable animations, draw system (before I discovered F5) and overly high encounter rate.  Yes there is a ability to drop that encounter rate but it should have never been that high to begin with.  There was more thought by the developer how to waste your time in pointless battles than put into the story.
The world and setting also feel very, very small.  You only visit a handful of locations, most of which seem to be overly large with a whole lot of nothing to do in most of the places and again seem to be designed in such a way to make you take as long as possible to go from point A to point B.  In any location there is usually only a few people or rooms that you actually need to interact with, the rest is just dead background space to make the world feel bigger.  Again F1 is your biggest friend, the same speed up in battle also works outside so you can get to your actual objective a lot quicker.
Also for the Triple Triad fans like me, this game couldn't make that experience any more frustrating.  The Random rule seems to spread like wildfire and by the end way to many places were using the random rule.  Yes there is a way to avoid that by playing certain NPCs in a very specific order, but again that should never be a thing.  Triple Triad should be a fun side objective, not something that I need to a strategy guide to use to avoid it becoming a random♥♥♥♥♥♥fest.
SquareEnix has made some incredibly exciting, intriguing, enthralling Final Fantasy games, this is not one of them.  Everything about this game feels like an intentional grind fest to make you take as long as possible with the game which I think people interpret as Epic cause it takes so long, I just found it boring.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Postal 2 is one part video game one part social commentary and experiment.  Postal 2 asks the question of "What will the player do with ultimate freedom of choice?"  You can terrorize the inhabitants of Paradise, Arizona through malevalent sociopathic tendencies... or not.  You can turn a cop into a doormat using hedge clippers and urinate on their dying remains just to be safe... or not.  Nuke a marching band parade, or not.  Re-enact the Kennedy assassination with Gary Coleman, or not.  The player has every available chance for good as they do evil. It's a physics-heavy 2D shooter where stuff like hit detection is calculated by the PIXEL, and the physics really are the coolest part. You can blast enemies to beautiful bloody giblets with a multitude of weapons, drop bombs to destroy terrain (and soldiers) and when you're done bombing, accelerate your dropship to insane speeds and slam it into anything that's still moving, creating a deadly explosion of fire and shrapnel.

With it's amazing shooting and an ai still unmatched today, F.E.A.R. shows that some games can age like wine.
Gameplay- The shotting isn't one bit awkward, although having true ironsights would have been nice. The ai, as stated before, is probably the best in shooting history. Instead of running at you in a line, enemies will often form formation around, while also waiting for you to make the first move. This is a great breathe of fresh air after playing Call of Duty singleplayer for so long. My one true complaint is that ammo for certain guns (in this case the pistol) where way to far and few between. Making you have to pick the specific guns it actually gives ammo for.
Story- The story is nothing fantastic, but it's still a lot of fun uncovering the mystery throughout the game. My only complaint is how the pacing was just everywhere. I often had to stop playing completely and remember who or what I was looking at. Whatever the case, it's greatly above average, and one I want to continue, but it can feel rather boring when in game.
Enjoyment- The game knows what it's good at, and that's small areas with multiple open spots on you at all times. This makes the shooting much more intense. But the same thing over and over gets pretty boring. So I suggest playing this game in sessions as I did. In the end though, I had a great and rewarding experience that I would recomend to anyone.
Who Should Play This- If you like shooters, play this. Especially if you like linear shooters, for example, the Metro series. While some consider being linear as a bad thing, it allows for much more intesne and challenging encounters, which F.E.A.R. absolutely nailed.
Number Score- 8.5/10

I have never been much of a fan of these sorts of games, but given that I've seen them pass by from the Acorn BBC Microcomputer, ATARI game consoles, the PC and just about any platform in between, and I was given a free copy from a friend I though I owed it to him and the genre to give it another try.
This game surprised me in that its controls are a lot more subtle than I generally found in most of these games; Usually in a game like this it's assumed a truck can be controlled in mid-air just as easy as an acrobat can... There is still some control but it isn't overly sensitive. Which leads me to the physics, which really shine in this game, even at high speed and the graphics being what they are (awesome in my oppinion), especially when jumping / landing. The music isn't terrible, but isn't great either. It doesn't hurt the general feel or flow of the game.
I have had some problems though; Game crash when select Own Score from the Leaderboards after a match, which also prevents me from getting to the Friends Score list. Not much into those online scoring stuff but I can see how others may feel differently.
And then there is the incorrect keyboard diagram shown during loading of a level, which marks A and S as movement keys in mid-air, which is kind of misleading (W and D should also be in there, although I never actually found A and D to be doing anything...).
It took me a while to figure out how to collect stars (which unlock tracks, arenas and other gamemodes) and the objective in for instance a Jump game; Do I perform stunts, height or distance? Couple of tries before I realized it was distance...
Sometimes it does tend to crash for no apparent reason, but the game is saved often enough and it is quite fast in starting back up.
All in all a great game, has some issues, but nothing major.

EDIT: Aug 31, 2017:
---------------------------------------
It's been a year and Stellaris has grown as a game considerably. The addition of Utopia bringing Traditions and Ascension perks make the early game a little more rewarding, while improving the late game via some really powerful perks. Countless balance changes have changed fleet compositions wildly, and new events make the game more flavorful than ever.
However. there is one big caveat. Unity, Traditions, and Ascensions highlight a huge issue with the AI. Namely that they have yet another way to fall behind. Due to suboptimal ship designs, horrible building prioritization, and the inability to keep Tradtions on track due to a lack of Unity production mean that a mildly competent player can run circles around even an "Insane" difficulty AI.
That said, do I still recommend Stellaris? For the most part yes. Stellaris will always shine as a roleplaying 4X before anything else. I look forward to further support for this game and will be aiming to 100% the game for the third time with the new expansion.
Original Review:
----------------------------------------
Let's be clear. Stellaris is far from perfect. Tons of balance issues, a samey early game, a barren late game.
That said, Stellaris has a huge amount of potentional. If the game recieves half of the support that EUIV and CK2 have been given over the years, it'll possibly be the best Space 4X on the market.
Highly Recommened that you play with Hyperlanes only and optionally a mod to remove Jump Drives.

After almost 5 months of crawling through dark sewers, rummaging through the pockets of dead men, not cleaning my house and being late for work on several occasions, I completed the epic adventure and moral journey that is... Deus Ex.

Even though it was released way back in 2000, and had never been considered pretty, I'd found that most well honed gamers still revered Deus Ex as a quintessential, almost religious-like, gaming experience... something I'd never experienced before (in anything.)
So, sometime around the beginning of the year, I crawled into the skin of one J.C.Denton, spy guy.
Deus Ex wasn't a difficult game for me (especially set on 'easy'), but it was challenging.  To spill blood or not to spill blood? (I'm a natural born spiller.) Should I  help the crazy lady find her cat? (I didn't.) Am I to go east or west? (I usually just turned left.) Will these decisions make a difference, somehow? *shrug*
Deus Ex  was a game of Nerves and Patience and Decisions... and bullets.
But, especially, Decisions.. which, by game's end, had become pretty monumental.
Yeah, I really can't say that I had heaps-o'-fun playing Deus Ex. Sometimes it felt long and grueling. Or dark and oppressing.
But, then, that's how it is, when something is intelligent and thought provoking.  And that's why I kept playing, because.. well, it was the object of the game.  I felt that, if I could make it to the end, I might, somehow, come out better than when I started.
And, I think I did.

This is an excellent and fun first person game that prides itself on tasteless humor and low-polygon violence.
In this game, you play as The Postal Dude, who is given a few tasks to complete each day.  You're thrown into an open world and required to complete all of these tasks in any order by any means.  While in the middle of some tasks though, groups of people, anywhere from violent video game protesters to Al Qaeda, will become outraged and attack you.

My all-time favorite mainline Final Fantasy game. It has a great story, lovable characters, an interesting setting, a lot of style and a better magic system than it often gets credit for. It rewards you for holding onto certain spells, for the stat buffs they offer, rather than wasting them at every given opportunity. The story itself has an almost gothic fairy tale-like vibe to it, although its setting borders somewhere between the modern and scifi. It's fairly unique, in that way. The built-in card game is also a decent way to spend some time in the game.
10/10 IGN nuff said.
Really love this game! My first FF on PSX back in my childhood and for me the best part from FF series.

The main character reminds me of edgy OC's on deviant art. If the game had a scent it would smell like an ashtray, dirty socks, rancid crab meat, and despair. It's a masterpiece in its own right, really.

+ Badass cutcenes
+ Incredible soundtrack (if you install the Wines and Roses mod, 100% required)
+ Deep and complex junction system although unintuitive at first look. If you know what you're doing you can become incredibly OP, but it does require a bit of grinding in order to achieve that.
+ Combat is what you expect from a playstation era, turn-based. Limit breaks work only if you're low on health, they look nice.
+ Very rich and detailed visuals, looking for a more optimistic and modern vision (eg. Esthar City)
+ Summons or GFs are equippable pets that can learn vastly different abilities to enhance junction/battle abilities and much more. For example there's an ability which lets you buy from ANY store ANYWHERE on the world! Or to turn off random battles completely!
+ Magic is usable as a spell and as part of equipping as junction to boost stats. Limited to 100, the greater the number, the bigger the stat boost. The more powerful the spell, the bigger the boost. You can draw spells from monsters or refine them from items using GF abilities.
+ Main protagonist has nice character progression although it's slow.
- Not a great PC port, there could be great improvements to the game, still plays like a 2000 game.
+ Mod support that could GREATLY improve the look of the game, and more like the difficulty mod.
- Antagonist is not presented as very relatable and hateble, just an average final fantasy villain.
- Monsters level with you, some people might enjoy this, I didn't.
- Story starts decent but rapidly begins being convoluted and only at the end it sort of makes sense. It does appear absurd at times even though it's Final Fantasy.
+ 30-40 hours long game, 50 if you decide to grind like I did, overall difficulty: easy if you know how the game works. Can become difficult if you don't know anything about the junction system.
Lots of violence, lots of racist jokes, lots of dark humor. Its pretty fun tbh. The devs still support it too so there's that

I enjoyed Final Fantasy 8 slightly more than 7. It’s not necessarily an improvement over it, objectively it’s probably worse, i just found it less of a drag to get through. I think it’s mainly because the pacing is much better, it doesn’t really feel like there is a lot of filler like there was in 7 which just made the game more enjoyable. The writing/translation is better which makes the long drawn out story bits less boring to sit through. I like the setting of the game more, the game looks better graphically and there are some surprisingly great set pieces in the game like edea’s parade or the train mission for example which I found very impressive for a game released in 1999. The soundtrack is amazing, it was very epic and it complimented whatever was happening in the game. I wasn’t invested in the story or the characters, the story had a lot of silly moments that took me out of the game, it gets really ridiculous towards the end in particular. I thought the story in 7 was stupid but this game tops it easily. I didn’t like the protagonist squall, I thought he was a very edgy, dull, whiny prick. They try to make him a sympathetic likable hero towards the end of the game but I just couldn’t care less after dealing with his whining for so many hours and I didn’t care for his love interest or the romance either. I think the junction system is a convoluted mess, it strips away everything the genre has built to create something that’s very abstract and broken. I did get the hang of it eventually but it was such a hassle to learn. The turn based combat ended up being pretty weak because of it especially with the enemies scaling up with you which completely discourages leveling, I just wish they kept their same formula but just kept redefining it to make it more fun. I did like the card game though that was pretty fun to play. I still wouldn’t recommend the game because the story is not worth all the hours invested, it’s still a slog to get through just less of a slog than FF7 was and this game in particular is pretty difficult to get into because of the junction system.

Cortex Command by Data Realms is a 2D combat and physics sandbox, featuring a vast array of weapons, bodies, rockets and so on. There is no real objective, most of the time you are trying out different weapons and mess around with the game's physics.
It's not a bad game at all.  For a while it's fun to fly around with your jetpacks, shoot stuff, and try things from the workshop, but at the end it's not much more than the rather unsatisfying slashing of the dumb enemy horde-AI.
If you are looking for a combat sandbox, try the Men of War series in singleplayer, where you can command EVERY unit with WASD (like in Cortex Command), but actually need a strategy (unlike in Cortex Command). If you are looking for a 2D combat sandbox, try King Arthur's Gold (Multiplayer). I occasionally come back to Cortex Command to blow up some bodies, but only when I am (mentally) too exhausted to play games with higher demands in reaction and concentration
It's not bad at all, and some will certainly have fun with the game, but there is just no reason to play it unless you are extremely bored  and have too much money.

I remember Cortex Command vaguely. It's one of the earliest examples of why early access shouldn't be a thing. The game was hyped up like crazy the first few years it was available. It was hard to be on the internet in the late 00's without hearing about it. People were hyped for a strategy game that implemented complex 2D physics. However, as time went on, the creator slacked in developing the game and lashed out at people who had complaints like "hey, it's been a few years now..." or "why am I paying $30 for $10 at best worth of content?".
Overall, it lead to the Cortex Command we have today. It doesn't quite work as a sandbox, and it doesn't quite work as a game, either. It's fun to screw around with for a bit, but honestly I wouldn't buy it for more than $5.

Certainly a brilliant game that i regret rushing through(including the 1st witcher) just to grasp the main story because I didn't want to dive head first into the witcher series by starting with the 3rd installment. That is just not how I do things.
Im just going to roll off some key points in no particular order:
All three games are considerably different and the witcher 2 IMO is actually the weakest of the three but I COULD be wrong since I genuinely did stick to the main story and the witcher is renowned for having side quests with decent depth and quality about them.
The witcher 2 is stunning graphically and harbours lush fantasy environments such as the forest surrounding flotsam with gigantic trees. A lot of the environments reminded me of the lord of the rings. The animations also far surpass its predecessor.
While the witcher 2 does grant you the option to explore the areas for each chapter, it does feel quite linear in progression. I did actually wonder off briefly once or twice to complete about 2 or 3 side quests and they were definitely satisfying to say im a guy who usually doesn't care much for side quests but who is trying to take more notice of them in the witcher series.
The combat is definitely more modern and fluid compared to the first game but its not quite as perfected as the witcher 3. I actually enjoyed the combat in the first game but ONLY after I switched the camera angle to high isometric to make it play/look almost like an ARPG similar in style to diablo 3 for example. It just fits the gameplay of the first game much more than a 3rd person person perspective but i digress...
CONCLUSION:
The witcher 2 is definitely enjoyable and while I did rush it a little bit, I did get the sense that it felt more like a putty of story slammed between the first game and third purely due to the linear feel and much shorter completion time. I reference my play time to give you a jist of this; [the witcher - 52 hours] [the witcher 2 - 26 hours] so the playtime is literally slashed in half. Please also bare in mind that the first game can send you off on so many "back n forth" errands which take up a lot of play time. So yeah, the witcher 2 felt more like it pushed you to progress the story but this is just my experience. It is definitely a solid game and I look forward to replaying it in more depth once ive completed the glorious 3rd game.
overall: positive - the witcher 1 and 2 are usually bundled together often in steam sales at an absolute steal of a price and are more than worth picking up.

It feels a bit redundant for me to recommend this game to people, but then again why shouldn't I do it over and over again and again.
Do you like FPSes?  Do you like RPGs with character and equipment upgrade systems, as well as pseudo-magic systems?  Do you enjoy multiple game paths?  Conspiracies?  Futuristic settings?  Stealth gameplay?  If you answered yes to any two of those.... Get. This. Game.
Deus Ex is a classic, in the sense that it is a huge milestone for PC gaming overall.  It seamlessly blends FPS and RPG elements of the day into a combined experience which resonated so well it became a standard in itself.  Newer games like Borderlands, Fallout 3/New Vegas, the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series, even Oblivion and Skyrim use much the same formula.  Deus Ex may not be the origin of that formula, but it is definitely one of the better implementations of it.  Dozens of games have tried and failed to recreate that balance of elements... sadly including some of the Deus Ex sequels.
What makes this game get such a strong recommendation from me though is the replay value.  Quite simply the game is so densely packed with content and secrets that you can have played the game for literally years and completely miss certain bits of dialog or secrets.  Add to that the alternate playthrough methods opened up by carrying different weaponry, investing in different skills, selecting different augmentations, and its easy to see why the concept of spending years playing this game is not far-fetched at all.  Don't let my apparent play-time fool you; I've had the game since it was originally released, and if Steam counted that play-time it would be in the thousands of hours.
In short, if you don't have it already, get this game.  Play it once.  Maybe it play it again.  Then, once you're hooked, get a mod that enhances and/or fixes the game and play it again.  Repeat for the next 1-3 years of your life at a minimum.  The last part is likely not optional once you complete the first two steps.

I enjoyed Final Fantasy 8 slightly more than 7. It’s not necessarily an improvement over it, objectively it’s probably worse, i just found it less of a drag to get through. I think it’s mainly because the pacing is much better, it doesn’t really feel like there is a lot of filler like there was in 7 which just made the game more enjoyable. The writing/translation is better which makes the long drawn out story bits less boring to sit through. I like the setting of the game more, the game looks better graphically and there are some surprisingly great set pieces in the game like edea’s parade or the train mission for example which I found very impressive for a game released in 1999. The soundtrack is amazing, it was very epic and it complimented whatever was happening in the game. I wasn’t invested in the story or the characters, the story had a lot of silly moments that took me out of the game, it gets really ridiculous towards the end in particular. I thought the story in 7 was stupid but this game tops it easily. I didn’t like the protagonist squall, I thought he was a very edgy, dull, whiny prick. They try to make him a sympathetic likable hero towards the end of the game but I just couldn’t care less after dealing with his whining for so many hours and I didn’t care for his love interest or the romance either. I think the junction system is a convoluted mess, it strips away everything the genre has built to create something that’s very abstract and broken. I did get the hang of it eventually but it was such a hassle to learn. The turn based combat ended up being pretty weak because of it especially with the enemies scaling up with you which completely discourages leveling, I just wish they kept their same formula but just kept redefining it to make it more fun. I did like the card game though that was pretty fun to play. I still wouldn’t recommend the game because the story is not worth all the hours invested, it’s still a slog to get through just less of a slog than FF7 was and this game in particular is pretty difficult to get into because of the junction system.

Stellaris is a great real-time 4x game.
It features great depth, complexity, is comfortably challenging, and features lore from multiple sci-fi franchises. Stellaris’ take on tech research is refreshing, its combat does the job (albeit uninspired), and the political challenges of ruling one’s empire are well thought out.
With that said, some of the planet maintenance is vexing, the NPC AI is shallow, and the game requires a great deal of patience. The UI can be overwhelming at first, but after a couple hours of gameplay it is devoted to memory.
I recommend installing a couple mods including: Auto Build and Improve Buildings, Resource Redux, and Increased Research Window Size. These help with empire/planetary management, resource extraction, and a minor UI annoyance.
All in all, I recommend this game to other lovers of the strategy genre (4x games) and science fiction.

If one was to ask what game I think was a flawless masterpiece, I would say Deus Ex is one of those games that would come to mind.
The general, non-spoiler-sih synopsis of the story is set in an dystropic, cyberpunk future of 2072 where there is a plague known as the "Grey Death" going around the world with not enough vaccine to cure the population, as well as the typical cyberpunk setting of the large socio-economic gap and rundown look to it contrasting with the technology present. You are JC Denton, a new, green augment agent working for UNATCO, an anti-terrorist organization trying to stop the terrorist groups, one big one being the NSF, and act as a police force. However, as the game progresses with its plot, all does not seem what it looks like on the surface.
A major thing that Deus Ex does well is the almost nearly seemless blend of first-person shooter, roleplaying, and stealth elements that this game has. With this, you have a large variety of choice of how you want to tackle the objective, ranging from going in guns ablazin' with a gung-ho attitude to being a stealthy pacifist who can take care of any lock or electronic system with little to no effort. Along with this, the levels are quite expansive and have a good amount of depth to them, encouraging the player to explore and rewards the player in different ways. The way experience is done is well done too, allowing the player to give free reign how he/she wants to play the charcter to a good degree and you level up how you want as you earn experience from completing objectives and exploration.
Now, despite the many great things I have said about it, Deus Ex is not without its flaw. One thing most will point out is the graphics (well, it came out in the early 2000's, I hope you were not expecting a whole lot in that department), but with the High Definition mod, this helps it out to touch it up (although not up to the standards of todays games in any way). Another is two of the skill, swimming and environmental training, having little to no use at worst and being situational at best. While it does not take away too much choice how you want to do your character, it is something that must be touched on to a point. Game is somewhat buggy to a point, as it was not as optimized for computers at the time when it was released. One other comment is the around-the-office-voice acting the game has, and you can tell how much they are Novice and green. However, I will go on the record to say that even if the lines come off as hilarious and cheesy one-liners, they are some of the best cheesiest one-liners and dialouge I have heard in a while.
If you are into Cyberpunk and into conspiracy theories, or if you want to jump back into the games of yesteryear from a break of modern games, then you will not be disappointed with an old classic masterpiece that still holds up to this day,
If I was to give it a score, I think it will be along the ball park of 9.1/10. The thing that stops it from becoming a 9.5 or perfect 10 is some of the bugs present in the game as well as some of the skills providing little to no use, as well as some other things mentioned before. However, you will not be disappointed with a classic gem at a low price!

A sincerely bad game.
Monster Jam Battlegrounds has 3 modes: Skill Driving, Stadium Events, and Stunt Mode.
Skill Driving mode is a copy of Trials (basically time trial mode) but with virtually no ability to control your Monster Truck mid-air. I may have done it on accident once or twice, but the buttons seem overall unresponsive. Seems like the devs didn't even know how to fix this, because your Monster Truck corrects itself whenever you're about to fall over or fall on your roof. The tracks in Skill Driving mode are totally uninspired and dull, with two different routes if you're lucky. There could be three on a few later in the game, but I honestly don't find the game fun enough to play to find out myself. As far as difficulty goes, the game is either very easy or punishingly difficult almost to the point of impossible, going so far as to include an "expert mode" which you are able to toggle if you want to rip out your own hair.
Stadium Events is what I would want from a Monster Truck game, that I sincerely miss from the first game of its kind: Monster Truck Madness for Windows 95. It's from a 3rd person perspective rather than a psuedo-2d perspective like the wannabe-Trials mode. The stadiums here are just as uninspired as the courses from Skill Driving mode, and the AI you race against has to have some sort of learning disibility, not that there is anything inherently wrong with that, but you will not find a challenge in Stadium Events. You will lap them almost every single race if you have patience when you hit your jumps (because if you don't you'll spin out). WHOEVER HEARD OF A MONSTER TRUCK GAME WHERE YOU WANTED TO DRIVE WITHOUT RECKLESS ABANDON?! Not only is it poorly executed from a technical standpoint, but it doesn't even follow the rules of Monster Jam. You may exit the lines on the race-course whenever you feel like it and you will receive no time penalty... not that that would even be a problem, since you could drive around the stadium twice and return to the course and you will still win the race. Anyway... Stadium Events had the right idea, this is what a Monster Truck game should be, not a bunch of gimmicks, but it's done rather poorly here.
Stunt mode is just Skill Driving mode but without a time limit or Skill, really. It has such thrilling events as: jump as far as you can, try to land in a specific area after you jump (different from long-jump mode, I promise), and crush as many cars as possible while you go through the course (this is far more boring than it sounds).
The Monster Truck selection is rather dull, with alternate paintings (skins) of several trucks appearing, such as three El Toro Locos and three Grave Diggers, with a total of 23 trucks. Why no legacy trucks? Maybe I'm just out of the loop, since I've loved Monster Jam for well over 20 years and many of my favorite trucks have been retired. Something inexcusable is that there is no Bigfoot. Seriously?
This is a short game, I would estimate I'm somewhere inbetween 25-33% through with a little over 20 minutes played.
Avoid at all costs, even if you love Monster Jam.

This is what I would qualify as a mixed review.
First of all, I understand fully that the game is being developed. That, and the very fun elements of the game that I have enjoyed have permitted me to enjoy what I got so far, and hope for more. The game is inventive and seems to be a great piece of work. The problems it has fall into three major categories.
1) Streamlining.
Its pretty self explanatory here, but when I'm trying to build bases or order soldiers / guns, it takes forever to navigate back and forth between the menus. You'll know how to get from place to place after one good attempt, but the actual act of manuevering is never easy.
2) Polish.
AI needs some work. The bots are at the same time both lethal to enemies and themselves. They're bad at following you,  but sometimes highly skilled at it. They can't hit anything for♥♥♥♥♥♥ one half of the time, and they're Rambo the other half. Some refinement would be much appreciated.
3) Glitches and Freezing.
I played this game happily with both previous problems until I was no longer able to enjoy it because the game stopped working. It would freeze during loading for around 5 minutes, then load the menu, freeze for a few minutes loading a game, and then again during play. This is a problem for any game, especially ones that aren't finished, but it needs work.
Still, after all of this, you should buy this game. Its hilarious and wonky, and sometimes a little unweildy, but its a great game and its worth your time and hard earned cash.

+ Gorgeous graphics that don't require the heaviest builds to maintain a solid 60fps.
+ Incredibly exciting gameplay with multiple abilities, skill sets, and strategies that constantly keep things fresh even after multiple playthroughs.
+ Memorable characters, boss fights, and action-packed cinematics that meld perfectly with the gameplay.
+ "A minute to learn, a lifetime to master" combat mechanics with multiple difficulties will keep you coming back for more.
+ Proper use of QTE's and specific unique sections create intensity that never feels tacked on.

- Issue with 1080p HDMI displays (typically TV's) that locks a true fullscreen display to a 24hz refresh rate (ouch) that causes a few game breaking issues in the prologue and ending. This can be easily remedied by running the game in window mode and utilizing a free program called Fullscreenizer to remove the border, however.
- Lock-on mechanic can be a little touchy at times when multiple enemies are assaulting.
- Ninja Run can be hypersenstive or not respond perfectly over jumps in certain instances.
- Topics that surround the main plot (nanomachines, Raiden's past, etc.) may be a little obscure for non-players of
canonical games.

As a life-long fan of the
series since the early days of my youth, I recall being quite skeptical over the release of this game due to the drastic departure from the stealth-oriented gameplay that us fans have all grown to know and love. After picking it up on sale years later and giving it a whirl, I wholeheartedly regret not playing sooner. The game does a fantastic job at capturing the overall tone of
all the while creating a whole new experience of action-based gameplay that can stand confidently on its own. While the port does suffer from a couple of issues, there is nothing that can't be fixed quite easily. It's worth mentioning that the QTE's are actually used properly, which is pretty rare in most games. The soundtrack could also very well be one of the best OSTs in action games that I've ever heard.
While not a canonical entry to the series, the plot is a very realistic assessment of what may have happened following the events of
. There are just enough cinematic moments to hook you in till the end - not too long, not too short. The experience I had felt like a roller coaster ride or a night at the movies - full of thrills, awe, and emotion. The fact that the game does not try to be anything else that came before it creates an entirely new atmosphere that supplements Raiden's character absolutely perfectly. While it would have been nice to see a bit more cinematics, I find that what is presented is really all that is necessary given the scope of the plot. There are a few references to previous entries, but they mostly feel like cameos to fans, but it may pay off to at least read about the plot of
before diving in to get a deeper appreciation of what's really going on behind the scenes.
Fans of other hack 'n' slash games will feel right at home on this one, even if
isn't something you're familiar with or cared about previously. Even if you're a veteran at these types of games, don't be ashamed to start on Easy to get a feel for how everything works (especially the bosses, which can be very unforgiving on higher difficulties). The combat feels extremely fine tuned and incredible to witness even on trivial fights, offering multiple ways to wreak havoc on your opponents. With the game's unique "Blade Mode" the player has the chance to slice up their foes and selective environments into as many pieces as they wish, creating uniqueness to combat in one of the coolest ways possible. The learning curve can be a little steep initially, but like most games of the genre, it only reinforces practice and grants an extremely satisfying sense of accomplishment once you finally prevail.
Packed with tons of unlockables and hidden collectables, the game demands multiple playthroughs in order to fully gain access to all of the abilities. Similar to games like
, previous unlocked abilities and weapons carry over to the next playthrough. Even with newly acquired assets, battles still require dedicated amounts of barebone skill to win. While previous entries of the series rely heavily on stealth, it is beneficial on certain parts to use the silent approach but it is never forced. The additional VR and included DLC Missions add to the replay value and can be fun to complete and master as well.
is an incredible action game that can be enjoyed by
fans and non-fans on equal ground. Even if you're the type of player who isn't enthusiastic about mastering these types of games, the story experience supplemented by blazingly fast gameplay is definitely worth a shot that guarentees a good time.

Stellaris is a large fish in a very small pond.  Despite a promising start, lethargic developers and a stagnant mid to end game quickly snuffed out the initial spark.
A few things before I put this unfortunate train wreck to rest:
•  The point of a 4X game is to be able to: explore, expand, exploit, and exterminate.  The common denominator?  Player control.  As such, I cannot fathom what the Paradox developer(s) were thinking when they decided to inject RNG like a steroid into literally every aspect of the game.
•  I want to do things.  Doing things makes me happy.  Regrettably, the minute a territory touches another territory, the game instantly becomes kill or be killed.  That's not doing things.  That's praying that my randomly generated homeworld and surrounding systems has enough randomly generated resources to create uncontrollable stations and uncontrollable AI troops to fight uncontrollable battles enhanced by randomly generated research.
•  When I found that single-player stalled out, I turned my hopes to a more rewarding online experience.  However, a plethora of unrefined and missing game mechanics makes multiplayer virtually pointless.  I don't think I need to explain how this annihilates any chance of a multiplayer game succeeding.
After 100+ hours of gameplay, I regretfully conclude that I can no longer justify spending any more time on this game.  The developers' inability to respond adequately to community feedback and prioritize what actually needs to be implemented/changed honestly is so disappointing, because I see so much potential in what Stellaris could become.
I truly hope that Paradox and its developers can get their act together and make Stellaris the 4X it should be.  Until then, au revoir.

Code World unfortunately fails at providing a good explanation of how computer programming works to people who have never been introduced to the topic. So if you do indeed "want to learn programming while playing [a] video game," some better choices are Human Resource Machine, Shenzhen I/O and TIS-100, although I'll be the first to admit that especially the Zachtronics products don't look much like actual "games."
(Then again, neither does Code World, which looks kind of like a collection of the placeholder graphics I created back when I myself was messing around with game programming)
Pros:
+ Interesting take on the programming puzzle genre (which is why I can still kinda recommend it, despite its massive flaws)
+ Soundtrack serves its purpose and isn't distracting
Cons:
- Ugly uninspired graphics, even for a game that was developed by just one guy. Just compare this game to the tasteful minimalism of Algotica, not to mention indie games that had actual graphics artists working on them, like Spectrum and Apotheon. Or just about anything you can find by searching for "minimalist" on Steam.
- Unplayable without a basic understanding of how programming in Python or a similar language works.
- I'm not through the whole game yet, but there doesn't seem to be an underlying story to the game. You just play as some ugly sprite that shoots messages at other ugly sprites in a series of completely disjointed puzzle stages that have no connection whatsoever to one another.
- Controls leave something to be desired. For starters,  pressing shift restarts the level, so you can't press Shift+Tab to show the Steam overlay. There's also no hotkey to show the names and values of the objects on screen, so you constantly have to switch between typing and using your mouse.

If one was to ask what game I think was a flawless masterpiece, I would say Deus Ex is one of those games that would come to mind.
The general, non-spoiler-sih synopsis of the story is set in an dystropic, cyberpunk future of 2072 where there is a plague known as the "Grey Death" going around the world with not enough vaccine to cure the population, as well as the typical cyberpunk setting of the large socio-economic gap and rundown look to it contrasting with the technology present. You are JC Denton, a new, green augment agent working for UNATCO, an anti-terrorist organization trying to stop the terrorist groups, one big one being the NSF, and act as a police force. However, as the game progresses with its plot, all does not seem what it looks like on the surface.
A major thing that Deus Ex does well is the almost nearly seemless blend of first-person shooter, roleplaying, and stealth elements that this game has. With this, you have a large variety of choice of how you want to tackle the objective, ranging from going in guns ablazin' with a gung-ho attitude to being a stealthy pacifist who can take care of any lock or electronic system with little to no effort. Along with this, the levels are quite expansive and have a good amount of depth to them, encouraging the player to explore and rewards the player in different ways. The way experience is done is well done too, allowing the player to give free reign how he/she wants to play the charcter to a good degree and you level up how you want as you earn experience from completing objectives and exploration.
Now, despite the many great things I have said about it, Deus Ex is not without its flaw. One thing most will point out is the graphics (well, it came out in the early 2000's, I hope you were not expecting a whole lot in that department), but with the High Definition mod, this helps it out to touch it up (although not up to the standards of todays games in any way). Another is two of the skill, swimming and environmental training, having little to no use at worst and being situational at best. While it does not take away too much choice how you want to do your character, it is something that must be touched on to a point. Game is somewhat buggy to a point, as it was not as optimized for computers at the time when it was released. One other comment is the around-the-office-voice acting the game has, and you can tell how much they are Novice and green. However, I will go on the record to say that even if the lines come off as hilarious and cheesy one-liners, they are some of the best cheesiest one-liners and dialouge I have heard in a while.
If you are into Cyberpunk and into conspiracy theories, or if you want to jump back into the games of yesteryear from a break of modern games, then you will not be disappointed with an old classic masterpiece that still holds up to this day,
If I was to give it a score, I think it will be along the ball park of 9.1/10. The thing that stops it from becoming a 9.5 or perfect 10 is some of the bugs present in the game as well as some of the skills providing little to no use, as well as some other things mentioned before. However, you will not be disappointed with a classic gem at a low price!

This has been a favourite game of mine for years. It's probably partially the fact that it was my first Final Fantasy game, and partially the fact that it had a vibrant fandom when I first played, with plenty of opportunity to speculate about just about every aspect of the game.
Playing it now, though, I still enjoy it, mostly for the characters. I know that I used to criticise the relationship with Squall and Rinoa for being out of nowhere, but I'm noticing that it really wasn't if you read the dialogue and pay attention to their interactions. And if you remember that, hey, these guys are all still in their teens. They're kids who've taken up weapons and been told to act professionally, but their brains haven't even finished developing yet. No wonder they're dramatic about it all and don't always do the right thing.
Gameplay-wise, I enjoy the fairly open world -- I've had plenty of opportunity to wander round and do other things than the plot, even by disk two. The drawing system is unique, and I've never hated it the way other people seem to -- but I can understand why it's frustrating (and also why it plus GF abilities can break the game: teach the refine abilities, get Curaga early, junction to HP, and you're set).
Triple Triad is infuriating as a mini-game; it starts out easy enough, and then you get a lot of horrible rules tacked on. If you enjoy card games with complex rules, or grinding back and forth between various cities to try and abolish terrible rules, then it's probably for you. I was tearing my hair out by the fifth time the Card Queen went to Deling instead of Balamb.
Also, a shout-out to the fact that this is a game from 1999, but there are many strong female characters, including in command roles (Quistis, Xu, Selphie, Rinoa, Edea...) and there are characters with disabilities visible in the world and taking an active part in things -- Fujin has one eye, Ward is mute, you can see people around the Gardens and in the cities using wheelchairs... Honestly, I look at Final Fantasy XV and I can only be disappointed by the sausage party; that game does not use its female characters to advantage at all. Why've we gone backwards?
Overall, it's still a game I love -- and I'd play the hell out of a remaster.
