is nothing less than a roguelike masterpiece. It stands alone both in gameplay and the
behind it (heavy spoilers in link), but still has remarkable replay value and visual appeal to anyone looking for a well-developed game.
As with any roguelike, a good run through
requires an impeccable blend of luck and skill. On the less-than-good runs, you'll be more challenged than frustrated - and depending on what items you may find, there is always hope.
Whether playing with the expansion or with just the base game, the biggest flaw is also what helps make
(and many other roguelikes) great. There are so many items and it is difficult to keep track of them all. What makes this flaw particularly bad, however, is the lack of explanation for a given item. While it is true that many do have some sort of caption upon acquisition, the fact that many items cannot be dropped or that the captions may be vague means that a player may be stuck with or having activated an unfavorable item. Especially with beginners, one will encounter an unfamiliar item, give it a test-run, and -
- you've hurt yourself. Some of the passive items (like the trinkets in
expansion) are too passive; they will activate only under extremely specific circumstances, like 1/4 chance of being active for a level or once every 10 rooms cleared. These items not only are often useless, but the player is left in a futile dilemma of which to take or leave behind. Instead of blindly guessing, a player may resort to viewing the
just for some documentation of which items do what. Many roguelikes have few enough items with obvious effects (e.g.
) or provide a clear explanation of what items do what (e.g.
). Neither of these traits apply to
, so new players may find themselves running the game with the wiki opened in the background.
Aside from the stated flaw,
is an experience for which no review can do justice. The dark humor and pop-culture references combined with stacking items and multiple endings makes a game more than worth the given price. The unique visual style may look to some like a cheap flash-game, but don't judge a game by its art; the story behind
, like Isaac's basement or a good chocolate cake, has layers. Also like a good chocolate cake, you won't want to stop digging until you've killed your mother and gone to hell.

Look. Games that are prone to scandal are bound to fail horribly. That's just how the industry works. However, The Binding of Isaac is quite the exception to this very strict rule, as it's very controversial, but very successful indeed.
The story's simple: Isaac's mom hears the voice of God telling her she needs to sacrifice her son to prove him that she loves him above all else. Just this kind of story can raise some eyebrows, however, the gameplay is what trumps it down.
It's has roguelike elements in a Zelda-esque dungeon system. You explore, kill enemies, get items, defeat the boss and on to the next dungeon. Each one is randomly generated, so chances are you will never have the exact run twice in your lifetime. As your weapon, you get nothing but tears. However, as the game progresses, you get items to upgrade yourself and fight a little easier.
Now I wanna say something: As a newborn Christian, this game repulsed me at first. How it utilized religion as a hardcore part of the story. However, when I saw the popularity of it (and the DLC came out), I tried it out. The result: I loved it. All of my complains went away from my first run to my most recent. So far it's the game I have spent most of my time on.
I conclusion, this might not look as hot as you may think, but you will change your mind once you boot it up for the first time. Trust me. It will hook you.

But if you reach that conclusion like most people would, by checking with witnesses, contacts, investigative resources, etc., you could have a thorough, airtight case that still won't satisfy the judge. The game requires that you've done investigation X while investigation Y is intended to make it more clear if you're hesitant to make an accusation.
It's a mystery that lets you approach the mystery from a bunch of different angles to build your case but only respects one of those angles as the true way to resolve it. It's reminiscent of getting stuck in a Phoenix Wright game where you've already reasoned through much of the mystery but struggle with understanding the tiny logical steps the game excepts Phoenix to make in order to catch up with you.

A straight FMV-heavy conversion of one of the cases from the 1981 boardgame "Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective", first published in 1991. You solve a case by skimming newspaper reports and visiting any places or people who seem like they might be relevant - when you think you've worked out the solution, you take it to court and answer a Q&A to see if you were right, with your score being the number of investigative dead-ends that you avoided.
It's enjoyable enough. The video scripts do a clunky but passable job of being written to work no matter what order you're investigating the leads in, and the British accents are largely terrible ("English toffee? My favourite!"), but flipping through newspaper clippings and following up on anything that catches your eye does a fair job of capturing the amateur detective genre.
I don't think I'd bother to play any more games in the series, but I'd pick up the boardgame.

You have to know that the "Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective" series is a game series that was produced in the early 1990's. Back then they were, although they barely could be called games, quite a successful series. Professional actors tell you a story, you are actually deciding only which story is told - you can follow even red herrings and wrong leads (which are quite costly in points) aim of the game is it, to get as close as possible to the rating that sherlock holmes achieved in a specific case. So you test your mettle against the hero of Sir Arthur Conan Doyles stories himself.
This is just a rerelease of the old series, and it's really good that those made a reapearance. Though the videos are pixelated (clunky) the game still has it's old charm. It is actually fun to follow the leads and try to figure out who is the culprit in the who dunnit. Let's just hope the rest of the series also makes a reappearance.
The Case of the Mummy's Curse was the firs in the first set of games, the story is quite well told - won't give too much details though, because you should try out this interactive "movie" and find out for yourself who was the murderer, and what other information about the victims turn up, and what motive the murderer had for each of his killings.
I can recommend this game on various reasons. First it's obviously a game which is thought to be a short sidestory, in between like some nice and tasty morsel. The acting and voiceacting of the artists is really good, given the time that passed between release and present, it's timeless to watch a nice interactive movie that was so smoothly added into a game. There are no complicated game mechanics that might disturb users, no hidden buttons, no traps and tricks; Just plain storytelling, interviewing and decision making.
Back in the nineties, the Consulting Detective Series was quite successful and founded the basis for a lot of other Sherlock Holmes games, most of them had to hold up against this series, which a lot of games, even adventure games with a lot more of variety couldn't reach the success of the Consulting Detective Stories.
It is a no brainer that I would recommend this game, alone for the nostalgic value of the series.

I will start off by saying that this game has very little to actually "do" in it, it is more of an interactive story almost, but not quite. The object of all three of the Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective mysteries is to gather clues by deciding on what people and places to visit. Once you have gotten enough information to solve the crime/s you will go before a judge and he will ask a few questions that you must answer correctly.  Getting to the judge and answering questions using the fewest amount of clues that you can will give you a score. The goal is to solve the mystery by using only as many clues as it takes Holmes to solve the mystery. There is not a lot of replay ability in the game except if your score doesn't match Holmes' once you have solve the mystery.  I wouldn't expect it to take very many playthorughs to match Holmes scores.
If you like Sherlock Holmes , or some not too hard brain teasers, you will enjoy the game. It is only about 60-90 mins of total gameplay in most instances for each mystery. As for the price, I would definitely go the collection route as it's almost half price. I would probably also wait til it might be on sale as well.

Don't be fooled by my hours, I played the Non-Steam version quite a while.
A lot of people seem to be confused by this game. They probably expected some epic story mode or intense multiplayer battles, and end up disappointed because CC doesn't have these features. But it has something different: An incredible sandbox experience.
Do you want to know how I play it? I load up a map of Skirmish Defense, enable unlimited gold and that my brain can be placed anywhere, then build an unbreachable subterranean bunker and start the game. Now the real fun begins. Wave after wave of enemies will try to tunnel a way to my brain, but this task is a bit complicated by the fact that I constantly drop crates filled with pineapple grenades and molotov cocktails on their heads and watch their bodies explode into gore.
Soon, the whole battlefield is covered in body parts and debris. The never ending waves of enemies have to crawl trough a horrible mess of blood and flesh from their fallen brethren, only to be ripped apart by the next crate bomb. If this gets boring, I set up a Sniper with a high powered Anti-Vehicle rifle on a hilltop. It is just too damn entertaining to shoot out a drop ship's engines and then finish the remaining crew with a single, multiple-body-penetrating shot.
The completely desctructible environment is just so awesome to mess with. When you fire bullets at the ground, you can see them traveling through the dirt and coming to a halt. The game even takes into account what weapon was used - bullets of rifles will bury much deeper than the ones of pistols.
This also introduces some interesting mechanics in terms of bunker design. Depending on the angle from where the shot was fired, a bullet will either bounce off a wall or penetrate it.
Exploding grenades produce shrapnel that rips apart even the toughest enemy. There is even a Chainsaw Gun. Guess what it does. Yes, it fires Chainsaws.
The only problem with Cortex Command are the lazy developers. This game has been in development forever, and nothing significant has changed. The devlog is updated twice a year max, and it's been ages since the last release. This makes the 20$ pricetag feel like a rip-off, since you're buying an unfinished product that probably will never be finished.
If you can pick it up at sale, though... go for it!

Just going to mention the more memorable for me and the less mentioned in the review.
+ The dust/smoke build up from firing on debris and objects. This is simply genius. A very interesting technique to use. Not only does it obscure the vision when you track and fire on a target, it provides cover for the enemy to maneuver, hide and reposition or get close and attack. Would like to see this in more games really.
+ The background music/soundtrack. One of the best that i have heard that makes you unease.
+ Game ran very well on Win10 for me. Unlike the expansions.
- Too easy. Too many medkits and vests. Easy to headshot the foes with slow mo.
- Communication between the replicas, AI. Really, they name this game F.E.A.R and yet they do this? Isnt the unknown a potential fear? Part of fear? Fear of the unknown? They do this at times even BEFORE you encounter/spot them. They could of at least removed this from the higher difficulties above normal but unfortunatly not. This is really a let down.
- Narrow maps, small rooms, few pathways, ways for the AI to maneuver or around you(entry). Easy to predict the position of the AI, especially when they are communicating and with 3D audio positioning. Only time i felt the AI "outmanuevered" me and gave me a hard time keeping track of them was in the expansion Perseus Mandate on the Train depo(?) area, map where the AI had several pathways to pick and came in from various entrys that was on the flanks while also a few from the front whom i guess was there to grab your attention(focus) so you would engage them while those who spawned from the flank entrys, did just that, flank.
Nevertheless, interesting game to try and find out what this AI matter is all about. But i would also recommended it for its background music/soundtrack that puts you in a state of suspense at times.

The binding of isaac is one of those games that generate a huge WTF sensation when you first start playing it. You start off as Isaac, a kid whose christian mom decides to sacrifice to Jesus because of reasons, so you run off to your basement to avoid the imminent slaughter. However you soon find out that it is not safe there either, and pave your way to salvation by shooting random monsters with your tears as you progress through the basement's labyrinthine array of rooms. Several power-ups and mom's items (and pills) help you in this battle, while you unlock more of them as well as several other characters with different abilities as you progress in the game. Of course,  you have no idea what each item does when you pick it up and I personally found fun in discovering different items along the way. The binding of Isaac's unique dark humor and artwork have made it instantly recognisable and strangely lovable among other titles of its genre. However it is a difficult and unforgiving game that will send you to your death time an time again.
+ Twisted -wtf- humor

It's a very fun game all in all, akin to something more like an old school shooter, there's only horizontal aiming, which feels weird at first since you do use the mouse to aim and shoot, but you will quickly set into this small obstacle. The game itself is actually very fun and can be pretty addicting. It incorporates elements of old school shooters with a few elements of modern shooters (reloading, only equipping two weapons at a time) that meld nicely together. The best part (and the selling factor to me) is how the game so successfully incorporates elements of traditional rogue-lites. Many things you'd expect from the genre is here- Permadeath with the ability of permanent stat upgrades, item randomization, stage randomization, and of course the ability to make the game unforgivingly difficult if you please, wrapped up in a first-person-shooter styling. Finish all that off with some simple yet pleasing graphics, and a large dose of humor (I couldn't help but chuckle to learn Strong Throngs long to belong and wear thongs) and you have a surprisingly fun game for such a low price.
If you like traditional shooters and/or roguelikes, I'd highly recommend picking this entertaining game up.

Having only really skimmed the surface of the game I can already tell Nex Machina is an absolutely glorious neon drenched blast.
Easy enough for anyone to simply pick up a play, with simple intuitive controls and a premise even your Granny can grasp (ie. kill all the robots and try not to get hit). But with a high enough skill ceiling, replayability and numerous game modes that even the most hardcore twin-stick fans will be eager to give it a go.
Housemarque seem to have taken what they learnt from Resogun in terms of creating a fun, colourful and fast-paced shooter and applied it all to Nex Machina. What's more bringing along the Godfather of twin-stick shooters, Eugene Jarvis, to help develop and refine the experience.
Admittedly a lot of people may find this game frustrating but it in a good way. As you curse that errant bot for spoiling your mojo and force yourself to have another go in order to "git gud", rack up a higher score and try and find few more secrets. And even to somone as inept as me the bosses do seem a little too easy compared to dealing with the hordes of enemies flying in every direction.
Also people are inevitably going to be annoyed that it only features local co-op but given the pace of the game and the need dodge those red menaces with pin point accuracy I can imagine online multiplayer (with issues of lag and latency) would have made this game a lot worse not better.
All I can say is if you are a fan of your twin-stick shooters this is definitely worth checking out.
As a warning, this game is experimental, weird, and a clicker game; but this is the best clicker game you'll ever play.  Also, the music is neat.

Nex Machina offers classic Bullet Hell gameplay with its own original style and retro twists. Level progression feels fresh and differant, complimented by an excellent nostalgia inspiring soundtrack.
Full of vibrant colors and lush particle effects and an intense tier based combat system. Depending on your difficulty you can choose how many "Continue?" options you are allotted (if any) on your play through. I thought this was a good feature as many players are turned off from the difficulty of Bullet Hell style games at times and lose interest after many deaths and limited progression, this helps to mitigate that barrier.
Overall movement mechanics, dodge mechanics, and collision detection are all fantastic from what I've played. I haven't had any deaths that felt unfair or unreasonable.
I highly recommend Nex Machina!

Stellaris. This is truely a space game. As it aimed for the sky and ended up amongst the stars. This beautiful 4x Space RTS has that one great thing that you loved from every other 4x Space strategy game out there all rolled into one. It blends mechanics from the likes of Sins of a Solar Empire, Endless Space and Galactic Civilizations, as well as many others. It has all the best features of these title with very few, if not any, of the draw backs.
The three greatest features Stellaris has over any others though are these:
Story - Not so much in the traditional sense, but events will happen as the game unfolds, planetary discoveries, meeting alien races, galatic wide events, that will often give the player multiple choices in how they want to deal with it. Lending the game some lite-RPG elements in that you can tailor your race to suit particular moral values and beliefs. Along side of this though, where some other strategy games get to that stagnant point in game play, Stellaris mixes it up by have one or two game changing events take place. These will quite easily filp the universe on its head, forcing the player to react and respond.
Races - You'll start a game with your own race, and how ever many other AI races to begin with. Then there are chance anomalies of new species and races forming on some planets. You can dominate these races, or help them grow, eventually turning them into their own space-faring race. On top of that, you have racial and belief divergence that if left un-checked will have some populations splitting from their parent race to form another. At the start of the game, youll see Team 1 and 2 and 3... by mid game, it's up to Team 16 and 17. And on massive games it can get as high as 30+. All with their own beliefs and morals and goals.
Soundtrack - This alone is worth the money Stellaris is asking for. It maybe not as epic as some other titles, like Sins Of A Solar Empires' battle songs. But it sets the tone and the mood so damn well. I've almost listened to it non-stop since, whether i'm playing Stellaris or not. It's peaceful, it's moving, it's thought provoking and simply amazing.
If 4x RTSs or sci-fi strategies are at all your sort of thing, then do yourself a favour... take to the stars with Stellaris.

I loved Witcher and Witcher 3, but this one sadly does not hold up in comparison.  A big part of my frustration is the map, which is almost useless at times, with missing quest markers.  The world itself is cramped and restricted and often relies on "fake" difficulty by making you run in endless circles looking for an item or location that would be a snap with a decent map.   In fact, half of my game time here is spent trying to navigate the map. I want to be out questing, not trying to find one of the three exits from a city that would be easy to find if they were marked on the map. That's not gaming; that's frustration.
There has been much commentary about the difficulty settings on this game, and with respect to Chapter one I agree.  Not only are you thrown into combat with multiple enemies right off the bat, your access to skill trees is severely limited so that you can't progress your character to suit your individual game style.  It wasn't until I reached level 9 that my Geralt finally started to suit my combat style.  Until that point, I had to play on Easy, and I'm an experienced gamer.
I suppose it was a mistake to play this immediately after finishing Witcher 3, which is about the best gaming has to offer, but instead of happy gaming, this one started to feel like an endless slog about half way through Chapter 2, and that's where I'm leaving it.
Skip this one and buy the superb Witcher 3 instead.

You play Bob, the most generic name ever, probably so you can easily project yourself onto him. You are a recent college graduate with a ton of credit card debt and college loans. As a recent graduate myself, I can vouch for having a ton of college loan debt, but credit card debt? I've never had more than $300 put onto credit. I'd like to think my experience is the norm. Otherwise - hooo boy. Credit Card companies must be making bank. The entire theme of the game has to do with life after school. You're kicked out of the home of your parents; which, being honest with you, I don't think is terribly likely. Most of my friends are about to hit their mid-twenties and they're still with their parents. Playing Bob, you advance your way through your career, your social life, life's many problems, and eventually conquer "Empty Life" - the final boss.
The story isn't terribly inspired. If anything, it's pretty much real life struggle. Finding a job, dealing with other people in your life, and dealing with real-world problems like depression. Most of the dialogue in the game is tongue-in-cheek fourth-wall breaking banter. Which, as I am sorry to disappoint you in saying this, does not make it any less cliche. It's amusing to read, but then again I also laughed at Tyrion's joke about a Stark, a Tyrell, and a Lannister entering a bar. My sense of humour is probably not the best to go by. Long story short - it's a JRPG that's aware of itself being a JRPG. Which doesn't make it any better.
Can we talk about JRPGs? Let's talk about JRPGs. JRPG has to be the type of game I like least, or it's waaaaaay up there. Why? Because JRPGs are long. Because JRPGs more often than not include grinding. They include memorizing enemy types (which we'll get to in a minute). They include all of this bananas stuff. I don't like the idea of levels, wherein you lose because you quoted bigger numbers at the other person. This is why I often praise Dark Souls. While levels can help, most of Dark Souls is about resource management and positioning. Very little of it is about how long you spend in the Darkroot Forest grinding Cat Covenant members. In a JRPG, you can be the best micro-manager of resources possible but still lose because you took on a Level 15 boss with your Level 2 party. It's a playstyle which promotes time investment of fighting mooks just so you can fight the boss. I just don't like that sort of thing.
My biggest gripe with this game is enemy types. As near as I can tell, there are three enemy types (possibly four). Those are Work, Personal, and Human (and possibly Illusion). There are a series of skills on each your party members which can be effective against any of these types of monsters. The problem is, you have no way of telling what type of monster it is by looking at it. So you spend half the fight guessing which type is super effective until you find it and then you have to memorize it for future battles. Suppose you leave and fight other stuff in another area of the game. Fighting this other stuff is pretty rough, so you decide to grind back in the original area. Now you have to try to remember what type of enemies these were. It's madness! It's bonkers! This is not what I call fun!
Every item in the game, every piece of equipment is related to real life but effectively it's a Find/Replace of your typical JRPG. Instead of 'weapon' you have 'goals'. Instead of 'armour' you have 'community'. It's not terribly interesting and it doesn't add anything to the genre. You don't get points in the game's favour just because you know what a Find/Replace function does. I mean, it's amusing for the first two seconds but when you realize what has been done, the chuckle dies down inside and you slowly come to terms with your depressing life, unemployment, and lack of ambition.... what was I saying again?
The game presses out three things that fulfill you in life. These three things are home, lack of debt, and marriage. You have to have all three things to challenge the boss. Lack of debt I can maybe understand. I mean, who wants to spend their entire life effectively making nothing because every dime they make goes to someone else (college debt is slowly encroaching on me...). A home? Yeah, sure. I can maybe get behind that too. Not having to be accountable to someone else for the state of your home is pretty nice. I like being able to put a nail in my wall without having to fill out some paperwork for my landlord as much as the next person. But marriage? This is where I draw the line. Allow me to bring up a personal anecdote.
In my senior year of high school, in my European history class, everyone was forced to read The Power of One by Bryce Courtenay. At some point or another, we were split into groups and tasked with the job of creating an alternate ending to the book. So this was probably after we had all finished the book. Well, I say 'we' very operatively. I don't recall ever personally finishing the book because I just didn't care anymore. I know protagonist kills one of his former tormentors and I think he goes to prison but I'm not sure what I'm supposed to get out of this. So we're talking about alternate endings and I can't remember what my ideas focused on, probably PK's boxing career, and another member of the group keeps trying to press this one idea. She agreed with everything else we said, whatever it was, but she kept trying to tack on a marriage. To the♥♥♥♥♥♥mentioned at the beginning of the book, oddly enough. I think she was referred to as 'Couchy' or something? Because everyone lays on her at some point or another? This partner of mine kept trying to force this marriage into the ending somehow as if that were the defining characteristic of a happy ending. Marriage. I'm not denying that marriage can probably make you happy (considering that I've never been married or even in a relationship in which marriage seems like a likely outcome) but I wouldn't make it a prerequisite. So that's a drag.
Oh, and this one comment is for the easily triggered: I did not find any way to have a homosexual relationship. Make of that what you will.
All in all, the game is decent enough to pass time, but I wouldn't really want to play it? Like, if you have a long car ride and can somehow play Steam games on your phone (maybe in the future... future... future...) it wouldn't be that bad but then I think - there are a ton of better games that I would rather be playing. So why play this one? If you like the snarky-sarcastic theme; some might even call it snarcastic. Though I'm not entirely sure whether snarky and sarcastic are synonyms. I can't recommend this game as a 'good' game though. It has humour... and that's about it. And humour can't carry a game like this. It worked in The Stanley Parable because the game was narrative driven and fairly short with multiple endings. It doesn't work in JRPGs because the bulk of the game is fighting, not narrative. So, sorry Cubicle Quest. I like the idea, but not the execution.

This "review" is more of a first impressions of the PC version of the game.  I've finished the game on PlayStation multiple times and purchased this PC version of the game because it supported Steam achievements and included a copy of "Chocobo World".
Final Fantasy 8 was the first Final Fantasy game I ever played and I love it.  It is my favorite Final Fantasy game.  It couples great story telling with great graphics (for the time), great background music and sound effects.  This game also introduced the card game "triple triad" which was so popular it continues to live on in fan recreations as well as in Square's latest MMO, Final Fantasy XIV.
The PC version has several advantages.  First off, the visuals are obviously much better.  It supports both the "original" graphics as well as scaled up higher resolution graphics, line filtering, etc.  This version also includes Steam achievements so you'll have those to show off to your friends.  It also includes "Chocobo World".  Chocobo world was a minigame that was included in the original Playstation version of the game.  The problem is that it required a "PocketStation", which were never released outside of Japan, so the vast majority American FF8 players never got to enjoy Chocobo World.
However, there are some bad.  It is quite obvious the porting was outsourced on this.  The original orchestral soundtrack has been replaced with MIDI, which really fails to live up to the quality of the original game.  There are fan made mods to replace the MIDI tracks with the original soundtrack, but why the developers who ported this decided to make this stupid change is beyond the realm of comprehension as far as I'm concerned.  There are also some bugged sound effects.  Quetzalcoatl for example uses the sound effect for "Phoenix" for 3 of his 4 sound effects when summoned, and there's no mods I can find to fix it as of right now.
I'm up in the air.  I would love to recommend this game, but I just can't bring myself to do it unless you just have no other way to play this game.  Final Fantasy 8 is an amazing game, but the PlayStation version of the game is superior in every way except for the supported display resolution.  Go to Amazon or eBay or something and find a copy of the PlayStation version of this game and either play it on a real console, or use those discs to run it in an emulator on your PC where you can upscale it or something.  The PC experience is inferior to the console experience, so do yourself a favor and get the console version of this game if it's at all possible for you to do so.

As far as engagements go, you fight guys on the ground with ranged weaponry, but you and them are made of paper, so you die almost instantly when one sees the other. Square Heroes is a multiplayer focused arena shooter from Australian Developer Gnomic Studios. In Square Heroes you create your owngenetically engineered killing machine that's only goal in life is to kill anything that moves, fight off aliens or even collect gnomes because gnomes are cool.
+Nice cartoony graphics
+Characters, both player and computer are well designed and somewhat remind me of BattleBlock's design
+Quite a few different maps, each in a different environment
+Quite a few different game modes ranging from Team Deathmatch to Gnome Hunt
+Lots of weapons to unlock as you level up
+Lots of character headwear to unlock as you complete achievements, each one has a different buff and debuff that goes with it
+Great AI with different difficulty settings
+Takes a fair few kills to unlock your weapons once in a match which means it's difficult for someone to get miles ahead of everyone else
+Super simple controls
+Bucket loads of fun when playing with friends
+No idea how they achieved this but even when players have a super high ping the gameplay is still super smooth and there's very little lag
+Nice music and sound effects
+Has great local co-op and you can still play online even with four local players
+Has a Achievement Hunter reference, as an AH fan this makes me very happy
+Awesome devs who are super friendly, very active in the forums and fix issues with the game very quickly
+/-The devs have focused on getting the multiplayer right and have neglected the singleplayer portion of the game, if you're looking for MP only then that's great but if you want some good SP too you might be disappointed
-You can't create private matches, kind of annoying if you're trying to play with five friends and a random player joins
-Apart from changing your character's colour and their headwear there's not much in the way of character customisation
Verdict:
8.5
A super fun multiplayer experience with nice cartoony graphics, well designed characters, lots of unlockables and great devs to back it all up. If you're looking for a fun multiplayer experience with friends I strongly suggest you picking this awesome game up!

Going straight to the point, controls in this game aren't crappy. They're abysmal.
You can work them out by practicing with wasd keys, but really they're a complete mess..
Basically you have 15 different levels with '80s arcade-like graphics in which you are a green square and must work your way out by avoiding enemies running back and forth preset movement lines.
The bad thing is that wasd keys aren't for movement, but they're for the ice puzzles in Pokémon (or Epic Battle Fantasy if you prefer): when you hit the directional key, you go.. you can't stop, and this makes everything or super difficult or super easy, depending on the level. You actually -could- stop by pressing space, but controls are so laggy and crappy that you will never stop in the right place.
On a further note, the game on my Italian Steam client/website has a translation which is the most horrible I ever saw - and they ask me why I play in English even if I don't like foreign languages..
The text goes "È necessario gestire il verde cubo e raggiungere un altro verde checkpoint. Ma è molto difficile, così come il giocatore interferiscono con lame rotanti e altri ostacoli rosso colore."
That translates as: "It is necessary to manage the cube green (sic) and reach an other (sic) checkpoint green. But it is very difficult, like the player (singular, sic) interact (plural, sic) with spinning blades (article is mandatory in Italian, sic) and other obstacles color red (sic)".
I want to meet the translator, he's my hero.
Anyways back to the game, it's a simple (not for the difficulty but for the fact it has only few short levels and you can only move from one point to another one) and standard arcade game; there are tons of arcade platformers out there that easily overcome this thing.
Get it only if you want the achievements, you'll find no fun at all. Soundtrack is horrible too.

Below you'll find a written and video impression on the game
Square Heroes is an multiplayer focused arena game where you take control of a square (literally) as it floats around the arena, taking out NPC enemies to collect the coins out of them. With more coins collected, you'll automatically upgrade your arsenal through out the match. You'll then take that newly earned arsenal and blast your player controlled enemies for points! It's an easy to get into multiplayer game that has a fair amount things to collect and upgrade as you play.
The game features a cartoony aesthetic with hilariously expressive characters, with a vibrant and bright color pallet. It also offers a variety of game modes to play through, such as death match, team death match, capture points, and survival. There's also lots of incentive to replay as you can upgrade your weaponary, as well as earning new cosmetic items to add in that extra spice of flavor.
The game is definitely multiplayer focused. The single player that is available is little more than a basic tutorial to teach you the game's mechanics. The single player in the game to be honest isn't all that engaging, it's all about shooting your friends and strangers online. That's where the potential problems may come. Though the game itself is quite fun when playing with real people, it can be difficult finding any one online to play it. From my experience with the game on day one of it's release, I've had over a dozen games and only about 2-3 of those games had actual players in them. The majority of my experience were with bots. This isn't really a negative point on the game itself, but is something people need to be aware of before investing money into Square Heroes. If you have a group of friends who are willing to all get the game, you'll have fun. If this impression is incorrect by the time you read this, and the game explodes in it's player base, then you'll have fun. BUT if the game still has the same population online when I played it, it can get a little boring playing with bots 80-90% of the time
Overall Square Heroes has some interesting ideas, my favorite being the arms race in the beginning to mid portion of any given match, and can be a whole lot of fun with some friends or strangers you'll meet online. But be aware, the game is relatively mundane when playing with bots, and from my experience with it, there were more bots than players online. I really hope that changes because I think Square Heroes has some real potential
Pros:
- The arms race mechanic is very interesting and a lot of fun
- Lots to collect and upgrade
- Very accessible and easy to learn
- Good aesthetics
Cons:
- (from my experience) low online population
- Might be too simple for some

Unless you have some friends to play Square Heroes with I can't recommend it.
The game's single player campaign is quite poor; it's nothing more than a tutorial due to the poor AI. The online scene is practically dead, I've tried several times to find games online and have had little success, the "Online Players' counter has yet to reach over 10.
Outside of that glaring issue, the game really is a bunch of fun. A twin stick shooter that is easy to pick up and play with friends with tonnes of fun to be had. As you play you level up and get new weapons and guns which keep things fresh while still feeling balanced. The basic levels design and gameplay allow for a really easy pick-up and play style of game, allowing it to cater for the hardcore and casual crowd.
Each round starts off with just a melee weapon, as you play the match out you get gold which is then used to unlock the next tier of weapons. It's a little snowbally at times but that just adds to the fun and intensity! You’ll be screaming as you rush for capture points, get massive killing sprees or lose all the money you saved up for that next tier of weapons! You have your usual Death Match, TDM and KOTH game modes.
If you really want to get the most out of this make sure you have some friends to play along with. It supports local multiplayer so it might not be bad just to pick it up for the odd occasion you have some friends over. Really I can only recommend it on that basis, otherwise it might be best just to pass on it for now and wait for a sale where it’ll get picked up and hopefully bolster the online scene, even if only for a couple of days.

I played this game when it first came out in 2005 and thought it suffered greatly from being released a year after Half Life 2.  Half Life set the bar so high that I couldn't help but be disappointed by FEAR.
After revisiting the game recently, my opinion has changed somewhat.  I found the game quite enjoyable my second time around (once I was able to get it running properly on my current setup).  I did have some issues with my mouse at times, but was able to get those rectified through the FEAR community.
It's basically a linear horror based FPS (and could possibly be considered by some to be the original in that genre).
The horror elements are neat and do a good job of breaking up the run and gun segments, though the spacing of these "horror" portions becomes predictable.  You'll learn quickly when to expect a jump scare which makes them ineffective for the most part.  I also thought that the horror portions would have had more impact had the story not been so convoluted and hard to follow.  In the end I didn't care who I was killing or why.
The gunplay and slo-mo ability is really where this game shines.  The AI is decent and challenging.  A strategic approach to combat versus guns ablaze is the best approach and that is a welcome feature.
I'll give this a 7 out of 10.  My 2005 experience would have been about a 4 out of 10.

So... this game is a bit of an oddball.
It tries to combine the (original)Doom-esque shooting and maps with roguelikes(thus RPG elements are plentiful). But does it succeed?
In my opinion, yes. Although the levels themselves are a step away from Doom and a step closer towards Wolfenstein - that is, there are no vertical elements, other than doors, that actually move; although the sprites themselves are not particularly eye-candy; although the rpg elements sometimes feel shoved down the player's throat; the game is still worth playing.
But wait, you ask, with so many downsides to it, how the actual cookie is Rogue Shooter worth playing? To it, I say it has even more upsides.
The levels are proceduraly generated, the enemies are randomly spread throughout the map. There is no puny cover system and self-regenerating health. No, the gameplay is high-octane, much like the 1993's Doom was. You are forced to get out there and fight, run and gun style.
The RPG elements, as I said, are abundant. There is metagame progression, there is in-game progression. The perks that you buy with points gained from levelling up give you all sorts of useful utillities, from crafting bonuses(yes, there's crafting) to map revealing. The metagame progression system saves you from analysis paralysis when you first jump into the game and are overwhelmed by lists of different perks and character traits(I'm looking at you, Cataclysm: DDA!).
What really tickles my fancy are the items. There are lots of different guns, from simple pistols and your sturdy boots, to overpowered shotguns and sharp katanas. There is also some equipment like caps or helments, and some consumables - grenades, stimulants, decoys. You are also required to eat rations to stay alive, though I did not find this particular element very entertaining.
What I did enjoy, though, was the upgrade system. Every(almost?) piece of equipment has a number attached to it. In a simple, RPG-ish way it gives you an idea of how good the item is in comparision to the basic template, like Machine Gun +1. The number can be raised by using tools while in the periodically occuring saferooms(I won't be getting into the economy of the game here, as it steps into the guide material). The equipment can also have different "enchantments"(for the lack of a better word) that give it unique abillities, like making you consume your hunger points slower.
All in all, the game is worth the price, especially if you are into the whole old-school shooter genre. If you're not, you might still want to give this game a chance. After you break the initial feeling of "whatisthisallaboutandwhydidIdie" the game becomes more and more entertaining as you play.

Deus Ex is a game that most of you should know already. It is a game that revolutionized the FPS genre as the original "Thinking Man's Shooter". It was groundbreaking in every single aspect, from the open-ended gameplay to the storytelling to the RPG elements it borrowed.
Basically, Deus Ex is an FPS with some RPG elements added on to give your character a better sense of progression. You start off as just another agent but as you improve your skills and acquire new implants you become a truly unstoppable force.
The maps are huge and sprawling with tons of enemies and civilians and there is never just one way of going about accomplishing your objectives. Everywhere is littered with secret tunnels, hidden stashes, locked doors, automated defenses and patrolling sentries. Although the storyline isn't quite open enough to say that every game plays differently you can safely say that each map has hundreds of different ways to complete it.
The storyline will from the start seem like a classic cops vs. terrorists but as you progress through the game you will find that nothing what it seems and nobody is who they pretend to be. You will find that your actions have real tangible gameplay consequences as you decide who should die and who should live and there are many surprises waiting for you down the line.
It's not a game that holds your hand and tells you who to kill and who to spare, more often than not a first time player will allow his enemies to live never realizing that there are real consequences and rewards to putting a gun to their head and ending their existence right there. Similarly there are those who can be spared or saved from death that will come back to help you or haunt you later in the game. This is all something you have to figure out for yourself as you play through the game and I wouldn't want to spoil it for you.
Although the graphics have aged quite a bit since it's release the availability of high-resolution texture packs and other fan-made graphical enhancements means it's playable even in this day and age.
Deus Ex is perhaps one of the greatest games ever released for PC and, in my humble opinion, the greatest shooter ever released. It's only real competition being from the System Shock games.
Truly a masterpiece of gaming and hopefully one day we will see a proper sequel.

This is the best game ever made. (IMO)
1. Level Design: Amazing level design! Each level is a new and exciting place distinct from all the other levels. The streets of New York, Edwards Air Force Base, an underwater laboratory. And you revisit levels multipule times only to discover new areas and paths you didn't see the first time. (Unless your a completionist and snoop out every path on your first play through.) It took me many play throughs to find every single area in this game. Some areas require you to play the game a certain way to access them and by doing so some other areas may not be available. So every play through is a little different. Which brings me to...
2. Variety: Every play through is a little different. Which route do you take to complete a mission? Which people do you talk to and which do you kill? Do you bribe the reporter for info or not? Do you play stealth or assualt or a little of both? What weapons are you using? What gadgets? What skills? What augmentations? How do you choose to combine all the different elements of the game?
3. Skills: Skill are a set of abilities you can develop for things like medicine so that med kits become more effective. Or you can develope computer abilities so you can hack computers and security. Like shotguns? Improve your rifle ability. Like to pick locks then develope the lock-picking ability. There are eleven different abilities in all. Which will you choose?
4. Augmentations: Augmentaions to your characters body give you super powers! The ability to heal any injury. To be able to fall from from any height and run incredably fast. Lift heavy objects or destroy incoming rocket and stop bullets. Hold your breath underwater for as long as a whale can. There are 21 different augmentations but you only get a few so choose wisely.
5. Music: The music may sound a little dated, but every area has it's own unique and memorable music that adds to the feel of the game. Each tune played adds flavor to the level you are in and makes the game even better.
6. Voice Acting: All the main characters have very distinctive voices that add yet another layer of depth to the game. And the voice acting is well done to boot!
7. Story: (No spoilers) A world wide pandemic, assperations of world domination, secret organizations, conspiracy, deadly mechs! The story will take you all over the world and have you make choices that will effect that outcome of the game. Who is the enemy? Who are your friends? Can you really know which is which? You decide.
8. Conclusion: Maybe you read this review and thought I have played games with these elements. Some may even be older titles. BUT, Deus Ex was the first to bring together all these elements into one game (particularly a first person shooter). Though much of this games features are now standard, they weren't at the time, not all in one package. I can't say enough about this game. If you have never played it then you don't know what you have missed. This game has held up well over the year. The levels may not be as big as what current games have, but the complexity makes up for that. Play this game today, it's not perfect, no game is, but it's cheap and amazing.
P.S. Before playing this game download the latest version of the mods "HDTP" and "New Vision" to update the graphics to a level that will keep you from cringing.  Afterall this game was made in the 1990's using Unreal Engine 1! Note that the Mod "New Vision" creates a graphical glitch with the regualr pistol, but it goes away after a level or two.
P.P.S. Don't judge this game by the newer Deus Ex games. Judge it buy the fact that there are still active mods for it after 15+ years on the market. That should tell you something about this title. I play it once a year. Happy gaming.

I'm going against the grain on this one because after trying out Aviator - Bush Pilot for the umpteenth time and being repeatedly let down by absymal frame rates, i decided to give this one another spin, this time on my new dekstop PC running on Ryzen and RX-470. I assumed the old laptop PC wasn't fully compatible, hence why it had camera glitches or maybe this game had been patched?
Aside from slightly wonky physics initially or maybe it's just my inablity to comprehend the proper procedure, i retried the first mission 3 times. Each successive time getting a little better at it. So the following is my updated review:
Note it runs stably at 60 fps. It's actually quite a good simulator, there's cockpit view but seems to be a little bit buggy 'coz it tends to move forward as if your face is touching the windshield. Despite that the cockpit view is still usable and steering control is surprisingly as smooth as Euro Truck Simulator 2 keyboard steering.
Cockpit view is not why it deserves to be called a simulator; it's the detailed operation of the towing arm that makes it authentic.
By no means is it an exciting job, it's about being patient and careful in handling others' property. So yeah in that respect it does its job very well and there's no other competing sims in this field.
The reason i think it got a lot of dislikes and even hate is because it's too cryptic. I myself hated it at one time not 'coz it's hard to understand but 'coz it appears glitchy. There is no guided tutorial, nor even text instructions. OK maybe there's a manual? Nope, not even that. The help is just a screen with icons with no text lables or hints.
Once you understand it though, you'll be pleased at solving the icon puzzle and quite impressed with the underlying physics although it can be a bit wonky at times. Would i recommend it? Only if you can be meticulous and like it slow.
One thing i'm very impressed with it is its stable 60 fps, something which Aviator - Bush Pilot totally fail to achieve at any settings.
Here is the gameplay and i'm quite pleased with it now so i'm changing this game to recommended status and a score of 6/10.  Definitely would be towing again.
The driving is ok and the crane is workable although not without great difficulty. But what breaks the game are the cameras' behaviour. They keep running away from the job (getting further & further) until you can't find the truck or see what you're doing. Save your money; the only reason i got this game is because it came in a bundle.
And oh, you can forget about the music, it's definitely not a selling point.

After pressing buttons randomly I discovered that F1 shows a handy little diagram showing which keys do what. Which empowered me to press on with this game.
Except the game straight up doesn't work. I tried for much longer than I should have to pick up that single car and got nothing to show for it. Except for a wanted level.
Yes. The game has a GTA style wanted level. Except there are no cops. Just a truly awful sound effect of a police siren. And from what I could tell that was the extent of your "wanted level".

This is one of the best games of its kind, possibly even the best spaced themed grand strategy game. Some quick observations from just over 75 hours played:
--> This game succeeds where others failed simply by removing the turn based element where possible and replacing it with the passge of time. Time is meassured in days and 30 days make a month, with a month being the equivelent of a turn in similar games. This seamless flow is probably the single greatest feature of this game (IMO).
--> Combat is real time and although you have little that can influence a battle once commenced, prior planning and unit design will determine the outcome.
--> Unit design in this game is great. this is not the first game to have this unit design feature but i have never seen it work so well. Basically you design blueprints for your ships and then may make fleets comoprising of many different ships designed to carry out a vast array of tasks.
Normally I wouldnt bother reviewing a game but this is a stand out game, give it a try. Better value for $ than most games oput there.
TLDR : Game is good, if you like grand strategy games, get it.

I feel like I have to clear up somethings on this game since recently there have been many bad comments on this game. Overall I really enjoyed the game and would play it many times to come. Now I have played Crusader Kings 2 and EU4, and I can say this game is not like them....but that's the point. This is a game based off of the syfi universe movies and modern culture have created. All of it is open to change, new features, etc. However, when it comes to CK2 and EU4, they  both are made off of real time periods and events. When Paradox is making a game off of a real event, they can add in the many complicated and complex features of running and maintaining a kingdom/empire. With sifi you can not do the same to it. There is so much variety and difference in not just the time period or the technology but in everything! You can not make every alien race act like humans because they are not human. You can not give them the flaws humans have because they are not human. The path Paradox took in this game made sense and is fun. What other game is there where you have so much control over an empire in a vast galaxy? If there are other games that are out there who try to accomplish that goal, they have a lot to compete with. A player can create his own faction from scratch. Deside from the start if this empire should be a warhungry empire or a peaceful city state in a waring galaxy. If you want it to be like eu4 then give yourself restrictions, make enemy empires that have all the flaws and assets of a human society. If you are too lazy to do that then simply open your mind to the many possibilities that come from being able to make an empire as large as a galaxy and embracing the lifestyle you want not what is programmed into the system.

Wow, I finally managed to play through this game and completed finally after only managing to get to the beginning of disc 2 way back when I was just a youngling.
I will say this title is majorly unique compared to other FF title's, FF8 brings around a new way of managing magic and customisation which is alot different to earlier and later FF title's.
Junction system, somewhat hard to get used to be extremely rewarding, this system allows you to customise your commands, power up your stats using magic and allowing to role certain characters into, beserk attackers, limit abusers, white mages and black mages, though not literelly there as classes, junctioning allows you to customise and use any character as you wish.
Magic in this game is alot different and though at first I did not really like it, i grew to like it and managed to find the huge benefits in drawing magic from enemies and draw points. Magic in this game does not cost mp, it instead uses 1 magic you drew, so for example if you drew 11 thunders at a draw point you can cast them in game in which the character draws it from.
GF's or in more popular FF terms, summons player a much biggger role in this game, these summons have abilities you learn via AP you earn in battles, these abilities learned from GF'S offer much more power from, junctioning magic to hp to boost your characters hp, extra summon damage from the GF itself, other commands such as "darkside" which allows a character to attack 3x more damage in the clause you take 10 percent hp off your maximum health per command. AP means alot more than leveling this game.
Leveling is not important this game, in fact it is better to stay lower level as enemies grow in level with you, AP gained from boss fights allows you to become insanley strong at low levels.
and on top of all the mechanics the fun system offers you brings you a really unique world and culture to explore, the story gets very good from disc 2 though but the gameplay should keep you going.
For a ps1 title, the cinematics are actually incredible but dont expect amazing gameplay graphics, though some limit breaks and abilities are eye candy (as is quitsis)
If you have played any ff title and are wanting to try another, i would reccomend this by far.

If you like Hack-and-Slash games you need to play this one.
Pros:
- My favorite "Spin-off" in a franchise.
- Perfect gameplay mechanics.
- Good story.
- Great bosses and enemies in general.
- Awesome Soundtrack.
- Fantastic visuals.

Neutral:

Overall Score: 8/10. Definitely recommend playing this game.
Story: 9/10. The story is outstanding. Not as great as the Witcher 3, but still very enjoyable to follow and will leave you wanting more.
Design: 8/10. The experience will take a little bit of getting used to at first, but is easy once you catch on. You have to plan a lot of your big fights before the actual encounter if you want to benefit from potions. There isn't an easy way to recover mid-fight if you take a lot of damage.
Value: 10/10. I only paid $5.00 USD for this title, but would gladly have paid more. Still very enjoyable even for an older game.
Controls: 7/10. Responsiveness to commands is a little more delayed than I am used to seeing in similar titles. Casting signs (spells) has me mashing the cast key several times before I get a response while it waits for the current character animation to finish. This can easily lead to your death in the harder boss battles. I have to try multiple times when opening doors and climbing up ladders becuase I am unsure if the command registered. You have to 'aim' the camera a little more than should be necessary to loot chests and corpses. NOTE: Key bindings are editable in the launcher.
Difficulty: 6/10. This is my biggest complaint. Easy setting has no challenge to it whatsoever. It is just a button mashing experience at this point. Step it up to Normal and the challenge is great for a first play through, with the exception of the bosses. Every boss battle is a complete nightmare. Most bosses can easily kill you in two or three hits even if you have invested extra effort in getting good gear and leveling up your vitality. The fights are very unforgiving of mistakes and will have you reloading your save dozens of times before you get lucky enough to make it through the fight. Stepping it down to Easy during these fights makes them pointless, they might as well just be a cutscene. If you are very experienced with these types of games, then the Hard setting will give you an enjoyable challenge.

Metal Gear Rising Revengeance: Better than MG Survival.
As a huge Metal Gear fan, this was a must have game for me to have and play. And even though it doesn't rely on Solid Snake, Big Boss, sneaking and espionage as the former MGS games, this is still a fun one.
MGR:R is a hack-slash game, where you play as mechanical robot Raiden, rather than flamboyant gay-boy Raiden from MGS2 (even though I still liked that Raiden).
The story is quite forgetable. President of some african place is killed, you fight the baddies, fight a modified, AI-controlled Metal Gear RAY twice, lose an arm and eye, get a new robot body with a metal jaw (why? just why?) to be able to kill the baddies. You then end up fighting a robot-chainsaw-wolf thing, helicopters, 8-armed red haired hawt lady, spikey-walled robot, a magnet 200 pieces ninja, the lady and ninja guys again, some buff af dude, a brazilian samurai, a crab Metal Gear, and finally, the all so meme famous "Nanomachines, son", Steven Armstrong.
The game makes you feel like a badass. The fighting is actually fun and fast paced. All the DLC is included in the Steam version, unlike the console versions (that I know of), which allows you to play as Grey Fox from MGS1, as well as do the JetStream Sam and Blade Wolf DLC's.
The Grey Fox sword is basically "super-easy" mode for this game. In the ammount of time that I have on this game, I have beaten it once as Raiden on Normal, which was fun. Then I have beaten the game 3-4 more times using Grey Fox's armor and blade, in the hardest difficulty. The game posed little to no challange, but was still fun to slash and cut through the baddies, pretending that this was actually Grey Fox in Shadow Moses, like that one cutscene in MGS1 (you know which).
Overall: The game is fun, though repetitive, and loses a lot of its challange once you have the OP sword and have it upgraded, even in Hard mode. But it's the only way you could ever feel half as badass as Grey Fox was in MGS1
(Can anyone notice how much I liked Grey Fox to mention him so much? I really wish there was an actual Grey Fox game)

Originally playing this at the PAX AUS indie booth late last year, I greenlit it almost immediately that night. Why? The concept is great, the graphics are simple, gameplay is also very smooth and flows well. Currently there are 8 gamemodes, including Deathmatch, Gnome Hunt and Last Alive, which have either solo or team variations. Survival and Kingslayer are the remaining two gamemodes, all giving the player a fun and challenging experience playing against AI or in Multiplayer.
Multiplayer is a huge part of this title, right now following the games release it doesn't seem to be that awfully popular, which I hope can change, as it really brings out the exciting, tense and even frustrating atmosphere. I played a few LAN matches with a controller on a single screen with around 4 people including myself and it was great, if you get taken out, it's not the complete end of your chances of winning. I must admit the snowball factor early into each match can be quite daunting, as players who collect higher tier weapons early can easily destroy any chance of you have of getting back into the game.
With enough players this game has the potential to become an amazing Multiplayer hit and I'm looking forward to the day I can easily jump into a game with others and enjoy the game to the point I know it can reach.
+ Fun, challenging and unique gameplay experience.
+ Multiplayer and Co-op.
+ I haven't encountered any bugs thus far.
+ Gameplay is very smooth, animations and effects are great.
+ Very easy to pick up and play straight away.
+ Tutorial covers everything you need to jump straight into multiplayer.
+ Playing with a mouse and keyboard is just as easy as a controller.
+ Trading cards!
+ In-game achievement and leveling system lets you unlock hats!
- Could use a bit more character customisation, maybe body shape changes, jetpack variations or facewear like glasses/moustaches.

Before you read: I Have played this games multiplayer for over 300 hours (~300h on my Mac and I just recently bought it for Windows). Just saying so you don't think I didn't play it a lot. Lets start
Black Ops 1 is probably one of the best CODs out there, for me it is even better than MW2. What I really like about this game is the time period it is set in, the Cold War, which includes the Vietnam war and the Cuban missile crisis. These topics really interest me and although these events are only really shown in the singleplayer campaign, the multiplayer (what you will be playing the most) is still amazing. Let's look at 3 parts of the game a little closer.
Campaign= As stated above, the events are set in the middle of the Cold War, they stretch from the early 60's to late 60's (not sure though). I won't give away the plot but it is overall pretty confusing, some scenes seem unpolished/unfinished but the missions are entertaining enough for you to forget the story anyway.
Multiplayer: You will probably play this the most out of the 3 major parts of the game. Here you can play against real players from around the world and with friends. Let me just say right away that you will get your♥♥♥♥♥beat your couple of first matches, don't get frustrated, get better. Once you are better, the game will be fun and you might get addicted. MP has fun killstreaks (Blackbird, Chopper Gunner, Dogs, Hind), great maps (Nuketown, Summit, Grid, Firing Range, WMD), enjoyable and satisfying weapons (L96, Famas, AUG, Python, Galil) and finally, almost no annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t (such as easy quickscoping, noob tubing, commando lunging, painkilling♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ target finder noobs, etc.). However the major complaint I have with this game is the inconsistent hit detection/lag. You will find yourself asking the game how the hell you just died when you shot the enemy 5 times in the chest and they turn around and 1 shot you quite often. Ghost and Second Chance are also annoying (both are "perks" you can choose to use in-game), but they are in other CODs too and they are not very common anymore (at least not when I play). Overall, best part of the game. To be fair, in 2016 there are very little people playing and most of them are sweaty max level nerds, keep that in mind.
Zombies: Back when it was good, simple, and fun. If you like killing hordes of undead, you can, even with your friends. When you are playing with 3 other players it is the most fun, especially if you are in voice chat. There is not much else to say, just try it and you'll decide if you like it, I will only tell you that it is the best zombies mode out of any COD.
That sums it up, best COD to be ever created by Treyarch IMO, decent campaign, epic multiplayer, and best zombies mode ever since. If you have never bought a Call of Duty game before, go with this one, it is much more pleasant for starters than say MW2. Peace out!

One of the greatest first person shooters ever made. At first glance, one might dismiss F.E.A.R, writing it off as yet another first person horror game.
When you actually get into the game, though, you will be greeted by some of the best shooter mechanics you'll ever see in a game. Even at release, the inclusion of bullet time was something not entirely groundbreaking. However, F.E.A.R has many other great elements that add to up a near-perfect experience. The AI, of course, is one of the most impressive elements of F.E.AR.
Enemies will react dynamically, and communicate in a realistic manner. You don't get the impression that you're fighting yet another generic fps enemy. They'll flank you, throw grenades, and vault over cover. They'll even dodge your shots! The best comparison I can give would be to the Covenant from Halo, but even they pale in comparison to F.E.A.R's enemy AI.
The inclusion of some pretty impressive physics also add a satisfying punch to your arsenal. You'll often notice papers being blown around, or lights being shaken. Everything in the game world will be affected by your use of weaponry. The enemies also have this over-the-top reaction to your bullets. They'll often be thrown around the envrionment. One weapon can even pin them to the nearest wall. Ragdoll physics were so satisfying back then...
The story, while sparse, is still something that impresses. I  often found myself poking around the environments in search of any background I could find on the events leading up to the story. It's riveting stuff.
It's just so great, and at only 10 dollars, it's a steal.
It comes with all the expansions, so it'll definitely keep you busy too. This is a must-buy for any FPS fan.

First of all, don't let the Metacritic score decieve you, it deserves waaaay better than a 44.
This game reminds me of those good, old flashgames where you pick your clunky, pixelated troops and let them roam around the map to invade and destroy the enemy's base, i loved those!
Well this game is one of those, but sooo much better in every way!
This game focusses on building your own bunker to protect your dissembodied brain from the hostiles invading it.
You pick your rooms, walls and barricades from a wide variety of different models and easily place them down.
Then you choose your starting units from a large list, ranging from zombies to T-1000-ish killerbots which you can customise freely to wield a huge amount of different weapons.
Once you've done that, you can switch to any of those units and controll them untill it gets eliminated or you switch to another unit. You can also put it in patroll mode to guard your base, sentry mode to guard a specific area and brain hunt where it will go towards the enemy's bunker and find its way to the brain. And if needed, call down a V2 rocket piloted by a drunk pilot who will probably crash, but still deliver your fully-outfitted troops roughly where you wanted them (or you just lob them from space in a box and let it crash a few metres deep in the sand, forcing them to crawl out of the gaping hole while hostiles throw molotov cocktail inside, fun times!)
I must say, this game is very fun to play, Its simple, creative and action packed!
Hell, i had a soldier once who faced off agains three other robots, his legs got shot of and his rifle got destroyed, so he switched to his pistol and killed all three of them before bleeding out.
It's these awesome moments that make this game so great! Shooting down a dropship and witnessing the soldiers under it getting flattend by it or a squad heroicly fighting off hordes of crash-test dummies while trying to block their entrypoint with a concrete launcher, and all of this happened in those few hours i've played!
Worshop makes it even better, adding in units from other games like Warhammer 40K or Halo makes it much more interessting, even adding in a few new maps is always fun!
The only downsides i've encountered is the clunky menu, the poor UI, lacking tutorial and the fact that there is no Free camera mode.
There barely is a UI besides the circular hold-the-right-mousebutton one which is a little confusing at first, the tutorial is very minimum, but you learn the basics of the game pretty fast anyways. And the camera, well, thats permanently focussed on the unit you are using, so no looking around the place, which is annoying if you hear a dropship nearby, but you can't see it.
But for my final verdict, this game is a must-buy for people who like customising their own troops individualy, who like games that tell stories about how badass the units were in that one battle against those 100 crabs and for those who just like building giant, trap-filled bunkers for the CPU to breach (which it will, he'll just dig into the brain's bunker right away)
I give it a score of 8.5/10, take that Metacritic!

While I do not enjoy Clickers, this one's got enough to make it memorable.
SPACEPLAN is a space-themed Clicker based on potato puns.
...
...
...
Yeah, that's pretty much it, it's literally a space version of the iconic Cookie Clicker.
The only difference is the cookie puns are now replaced with potato puns.
It has a story, but it's so ludicrous that I can't take it seriously.
For those of you who don't know what a Clicker is, Clickers are games where the whole objective is to rack up points by clicking on a single object, hence the name, and then buying upgrades with those points to earn more points.
They're simple, repetitive, and literally drug money due to how addictive they can be.
Once you start playing, you never stop since it keeps playing even if you turn it off.
The only way to stop it is to erase the save file. (this resets the game back to the start)
Each Clicker has different themes and mechanics, but they're all the same game at their core.
Most Clickers don't have an ending, but this one does and it's worth playing to see.
I can't really say much about this game.
It has a great idea for its story, but a Clicker is still a Clicker no matter how fancy you make it.
I'm only recommending it because at least some effort was put into it despite being a Clicker.
The game hints at the idea of a sequel, but this could just be a parody of a trope.

TLDR: TENTATIVE recommendation.
Pros:
I found this game to be a very good mix between roguelike and old-school FPS. The action is basically Wolfenstein 3D with more varied enemies, but the roguelike part comes in with the big variety of weapons, gear, ammo, mysterious consumables and crafting elements you pick up.
The author also has a good sense of humor. Those two words explain it all: dog launcher.
Cons:
I didn't experience any bug unlike other people, but I dislike the movement in this game as it's too easy to get stuck on corners while trying to strafe. As a Doom, Duke3D and Wolf3D player I don't remember having that problem with those old-school games.
I think this qualifies as a complete game, and people claiming it's "abandoned" instead of "finished" are crybabies and backseat game designers. This said, you could imagine many ways to improve it. Such as bigger levels with doors, so you don't get half the enemies rushing you around your spawn area, the rest being a simpe mop-up phase. Or levers to pull to trigger stuff, and so on.
Lastly, an element I dislike very much (STOP IT roguelike designers) is that you accumulate Intel between runs, a currency that you can use to make future runs easier by buying more health and other stats. This is grinding built into the game, and guarantees that the balance will always be off: when you start playing deeper levels will likely be impossible because they're balanced around a player having unlocked all the stats. When you have unlocked all the stats the earlier levels are gonna be laughably easy and devoid of challenge. Unless you increase the difficulty, but then you're back to square one. Remember kids: there's a reason the best roguelite games such as Spelunky, Ziggurat and Binding of Isaac don't accumulate player power between runs.
In the end despite its numerous flaws I had some fun, so I do recommend to pick it up for its uniqueness. I probably won't stick with the game for long though, when I have better alternatives at hand. Do try out the demo beforehand as some people have reported incompatibility with their hardware.

I love simulator games, but Towtruck Simulator 2015 gave me a head ache, both  as a simulation game and literally; I had to lay down and close my eyes for  half an hour  after playing this game.
The first thing that struck me was the un-responsivness of the controls.  It feels like you are travelling through treacle all the time.  Even though the speedo shows that you are doing   60kph,  you feel like you are crawling, with no variation in  the speed of the vehicle apart from when you first accelerate from  stationary, and even that was unrealistic.  All other vehicles on the road apart from looking remarkably similar (there was very little variation in color and only several different models of car, with no other HGV or  articulated vehicles  appaent in game),   travel at the same slow speed;  and,  if you happen to crash into  any car, despite driving  a  5 or 6 ton vehicle at speed,  the   car appears to be glued to the road as it doesn't budge an inch when you crash into it .  Cars   appearing in the distance seemed  to slide and even jump about , and movement when turning corners was erratic and unrealistic. Other vehicle simulators like Euro Truck Simulator 1 & 2  at least have  some modicum of realism (apart from actual crash damage) when you crash into other vehicles.
The map showing you the  placement of  cars that needed towing isn't very clear and  so far I've not found a key binding  that will allow me to  zoom in on the map, and  on top of all these issues  the whole environment looks drab and reminds me of what in game environments looked like  10 years ago, not  next year (as in the games title Tow Truck Simulator 2015).  Finally, try actually picking up  a vehicle once you've found one, it's not impossible, but  I tried and failed several times. There's a basic plan of the controls via the F1 key *see the last image link posted below), but  there's no actual  tutorial, so trying to actually pick up  a vehicle for the first time is pretty hard to figure out unless you have a PhD in mechanical engineering.  After playing the game for a couple of hours I  had to gave up. (I did  returned briefly  to  check on some points while writng this  review) .  In my opinion  Tow Truck Simulator 2015  was a  throughly unpleasant game to play.
Thankfully I got this game (twice) via  both Bundle Star  sim bundles, so can't really complain about how much I  wasted as there were some decent sims  games included  with each of the bundles I purchased.
You can see some images (taken by me) and a You Tube video posted by WhyBeHere below:
(sterile environment)
(Car park  carash)
(stuck in traffic)
(attempting to pick up a vehicle)
(key bindings)
After checking out what the earlier version of this game (2010 version) played like, it seems the developer  has  taken a retrograde step  in many of the game play features.  You can check this out yourself by comparing  game play from each game via You Tube videos.   In essence  I'd much rather be playing the  2010 version than the  2015 version.
e.g.
Other vehicles look  like they travel faster, the cars  can be knocked off the road if you crash into them which means if you get stuck in traffic   you can at least plow a path through  cars being driven along the roads if needed, wheras in the 2015 version, you easily get trapped between  oncoming   vehicles and vehicles behind you because of the   cars   being stuck to the road (see the third image above, I was completely stuck at this point after trying to extricate myself from  the vehicle  pile up ;......well, not really a pile up). The only way to get out of the game was to  restart;  game saves seem to be disables as I wasn't able to save my progress.    Also the collision mesh  leaves a lot to be desired, with my truck being able to partly  drive through  various  inanimate objects like tree trunks.
I doubt I'll ever  play this game again  because I've got much better   and more realistic simulation games to  enjoy.  Even GTA V (X-Box version) has a usable tow truck that operates much better and that's only one very tiny aspect of that particular game.
